    How to use this guide

    jump:start-howto

    Fast path

    1. Press / or Ctrl+K and type what you need, for example guest account or ufw.
    2. Press Down to pick a result and Enter to jump to that exact subheading.
    3. Follow the numbered steps in the Fast path box at the top of the section.
    4. Click a highlighted placeholder such as <username>, type the real value, then press Copy on the command.
    5. Press Alt+Left to go back to where you were.

    #Search the guide

    Press / or Ctrl+K from anywhere on the page and start typing. Results are ranked by relevance and each one shows the matching subheading, so Enter lands on the exact spot inside a long section. Small typos and half-typed words still match.

    Key Does
    / or Ctrl+K Jump to the search box
    Up / Down Move through results
    Enter Open the highlighted result at its subheading
    Esc Close the results and clear the search
    Alt+Left Go back to where you were before the last jump

    The filter chips under the search box limit results to one area (All, Windows 11, Server, Linux, Cisco quiz, Packet Tracer, General). Use them when a word like "firewall" matches every image.

    #Home screen and quick links

    The top of the page is a home screen with one tile per area. Each tile shows how much of that area's checklists the team has ticked. The quick links go straight to the sections teams open most during a round.

    #Round clock

    The round clock on the home screen counts down the 4-hour competition period. The same time shows in the clock button in the top bar.

    1. Click Start clock now when the first image powers on, or click Set start time and enter the time it powered on.
    2. Follow the phase line under the clock. It walks through the 6 phases of the round plan and plays a sound when the next phase starts.
    3. Listen for the alerts at 60, 30, 10 and 5 minutes left.
    4. Click Stop clock to clear it.

    In team live mode the clock is shared, so starting, setting or stopping it changes it for the whole team.

    #Fast path boxes, tabs and "why" blocks

    Block How to use it
    Fast path box Numbered exact steps at the top of a task section. Do them in order; the details and variations are below the box.
    Tabs Alternative ways to do the same job: GUI, PowerShell or cmd on Windows, Mint GUI or Terminal on Linux. Pick one tab. The first tab is the one most people should use.
    Collapsible "why" block Background and edge cases. Closed by default, so skip it mid-round and read it later.

    #Fill in placeholders once

    Placeholders such as <username> and <service-name> are highlighted inside commands. Click one, type the value once, and every command on the page that uses the same placeholder fills in. The Copy button then copies the filled-in command.

    The Values button in the top bar lists everything you have filled in and clears it. Clear values when you move to another image, because a Windows username left filled in will also appear in the Linux commands.

    If you type a command by hand, replace the whole placeholder, angle brackets included.

    #Copy buttons and checklists

    Every code block has a Copy button. Paste with a right-click or Ctrl+V in PowerShell, Ctrl+Shift+V in a Linux terminal, and right-click or Ctrl+V in the Packet Tracer CLI.

    Click a checklist item to tick it. Progress shows on each section header, in the sidebar for each area, and on the home screen tiles. The Reset checklists button in the sidebar clears the ticks in your browser after a confirmation. In team live mode the ticks are shared and the button becomes Reset team, which clears everyone's ticks, so agree as a team before anyone presses it.

    A tick says a step is done. It does not record what you changed or which score it moved, so keep a change log as well (how).

    #Sounds and theme

    The page plays quiet sounds when you tick an item, copy a command, finish a checklist and receive a team message. Turn them off or on with the speaker button in the top bar or the M key.

    The theme button in the top bar switches between light and dark.

    #Jump codes for Ctrl+F

    Every section header shows a jump code. If search ever stops working, press Ctrl+F and type jump, a colon and the section id with no spaces (for example the code for Windows users ends in w11-users). It matches once on the page, in that section's header. The Jump code index at the end lists every code.

    #Team live mode

    One laptop can host this guide on your local network so the whole team shares checklist ticks, the round clock, a team chat and notes on each section. The Team button in the top bar opens the chat. Setup and the rules question are in Team live mode.

    #Reading the callouts

    Box color and title Means
    Danger Can cost points, break a required service, lock you out or break scoring. Read it before you act.
    Warning A common mistake.
    Tip A faster way to do the job.
    Verify The command that proves the fix worked.
    Note Background or a side fact.

    #Opening this file during a round

    Keep the file on the physical computer (or a USB drive) and open it by double-clicking. It runs fully offline with no installs and nothing loaded from the web. Open it in a browser on the physical computer, outside the competition virtual machine, so it never touches the image you are scored on.

    Team live mode (shared checklists and chat)

    jump:start-live

    Live mode runs a small server on one laptop (the host). Teammates open the guide from that laptop over the local network and share ticks, the round clock, chat and notes within a second or two. Nothing goes to the internet.

    Fast path

    1. On the host laptop, open the live folder and double-click Start live (Python).bat. If it says Python 3.8 or newer was not found, double-click Start live (PowerShell).bat instead and click Yes on the administrator prompt.
    2. Python only: if Windows shows a firewall prompt, tick Private networks and click Allow access.
    3. Read the address (like http://192.168.1.23:8080) and the 4-digit room PIN from the server window. Leave the window open and do not click inside it.
    4. On each teammate's computer, join the same network and type that address, starting with http:// and including :8080, into a browser on the physical computer, outside the competition VM.
    5. In the Join dialog, enter a display name and the room PIN.
    6. If a teammate cannot connect, work through Fix network problems.

    Check the rules first

    Ask your coach before you use live mode in a scored round. The reasons are in Rules and safety.

    #What live mode gives the team

    Feature What you see
    Shared checklists A tick appears on every teammate's screen within a second or two, with the initials of whoever ticked it.
    Team panel The Team button in the top bar (it shows how many are online) opens a panel with Chat, Activity and Online tabs.
    Team chat The Chat tab has channels for General, Windows 11, Server, Linux, Cisco and Change log.
    Activity feed The Activity tab lists recent ticks and messages from the whole team.
    Who is online The Online tab lists each teammate's name and the section they are reading.
    Section notes Each section header gets a Notes button that opens a thread for that section.
    Shared round clock The round clock on the home screen is the same for everyone. Starting, setting or stopping it changes it for the team.
    Reset team The Reset checklists button becomes Reset team. After a confirmation it clears everyone's ticks.
    Saved state Everything is saved on the host laptop in cp-live-state.json and reloaded when the server restarts.

    Use the Change log channel as the team's change log: time, image, what you changed, score before and after.

    #What is in the live folder

    File What it is
    CyberPatriot-Field-Guide.html The guide itself. It also works opened directly, offline, without live features.
    cp-live-server.py The live server for computers with Python 3.8 or newer.
    cp-live-server.ps1 The same server written in PowerShell, for Windows without Python.
    Start live (Python).bat Double-click to start the Python server.
    Start live (PowerShell).bat Double-click to start the PowerShell server (asks for administrator approval).
    README-live.txt Setup notes in plain text.

    Keep the files together in one folder. The servers look for CyberPatriot-Field-Guide.html next to them.

    #Start the server with Python (option A)

    The Python launcher needs Python 3.8 or newer. To check, open cmd and run either command:

    py --version

    python --version

    You should see a version line:

    Python 3.12.4

    Any version from 3.8 up works. If you see "Python was not found", the Microsoft Store opens, or the version is older than 3.8, use option B.

    Double-click Start live (Python).bat. To start it from cmd instead, open the folder in File Explorer, type cmd in the address bar, press Enter, and run:

    py cp-live-server.py

    Open a terminal in the live folder and run:

    python3 cp-live-server.py

    The server uses port 8080 and makes up a random 4-digit room PIN each time it starts. To choose the port and the PIN yourself, add the optional flags (on Mac or Linux start the line with python3 instead of py):

    py cp-live-server.py --port 8090 --pin 2468
    Python flag Sets
    --port TCP port (default 8080)
    --pin Room PIN (default: random 4 digits)
    --file Guide HTML file (default: CyberPatriot-Field-Guide.html next to the script)
    --state State file (default: cp-live-state.json next to the script)
    --host Address to listen on (default 0.0.0.0, all addresses; 127.0.0.1 means only this laptop)

    The same flags work after the launcher name when you run Start live (Python).bat from cmd.

    The first time the Python server runs, Windows shows a firewall prompt. Tick Private networks and click Allow access (details).

    #Start the server without Python (option B)

    1. Double-click Start live (PowerShell).bat.
    2. Click Yes on the User Account Control prompt. The server starts in a new window.

    Without administrator rights the PowerShell server only serves the host laptop itself (http://localhost:8080), and teammates cannot connect. The window says so when it is not running as administrator. While elevated, it adds an inbound firewall rule named "CP Live Guide" (TCP, that port) for Private and Domain networks. The rule does not cover Public networks, so a Wi-Fi connection set to Public will block teammates (fix).

    PowerShell parameter Sets
    -Port TCP port (default 8080)
    -Pin Room PIN (default: random 4 digits)
    -File Guide HTML file
    -State State file (default cp-live-state.json)
    -NoFirewall Do not add the firewall rule
    -LocalOnly Serve only this laptop, for testing

    To pass parameters, open cmd and go to the live folder:

    cd /d "<path>"

    Then run the launcher with the parameters:

    "Start live (PowerShell).bat" -Port 8090 -Pin 2468

    If cmd is not running as administrator, the launcher asks for approval and restarts itself elevated with the same parameters.

    Check the rule exists (PowerShell):

    Get-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "CP Live Guide"

    Remove the rule when you are done. Run this in PowerShell as administrator:

    Remove-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "CP Live Guide"

    #Read the address and PIN

    The server window prints one or more addresses for teammates, like http://192.168.1.23:8080, the 4-digit room PIN, and where the shared state is saved. On the host laptop itself, use http://localhost:8080.

    If it prints more than one address, use the one from the Wi-Fi or Ethernet adapter and try the others if it fails. Ignore addresses from virtual adapters (vEthernet, VirtualBox, VMware VMnet1 and VMnet8). To see which address belongs to which adapter, run this in cmd and look at "IPv4 Address" under the Wi-Fi or Ethernet heading:

    ipconfig

    Keep the server running

    Closing the server window stops live mode for everyone. Keep the host laptop plugged in and stop it from sleeping. Press Ctrl+C in the window to stop the server; the state is saved automatically.

    Stop the host laptop from sleeping while plugged in (Settings > System > Power & battery > Screen, sleep and hibernate timeouts > set the plugged-in sleep time to Never), or run this in cmd:

    powercfg /change standby-timeout-ac 0

    #Join as a teammate

    1. Connect your computer to the same network as the host laptop.
    2. Open a browser on your physical computer, outside the competition VM.
    3. Type the address from the server window exactly, for example http://192.168.1.23:8080: http (not https), with the :8080 part.
    4. In the Join dialog, enter a display name and the room PIN. Your initials are taken from the name and mark your ticks.

    Use the host laptop's network address. localhost and 127.0.0.1 always mean "this computer", so on a teammate's machine they point at the wrong computer.

    If live mode is down, double-click CyberPatriot-Field-Guide.html to open the guide offline. Everything works except the shared features.

    #Fix network problems

    Work through these in order. Most failures are the firewall prompt, a Public network profile, or a school network that blocks device-to-device traffic.

    #Allow Python through the Windows firewall

    On the first run, Windows shows "Windows Defender Firewall has blocked some features of this app" for Python. Tick Private networks and click Allow access.

    If someone clicked Cancel, Windows saves a block rule for Python. Fix it:

    1. Press Win+R, type firewall.cpl, press Enter.
    2. Click "Allow an app or feature through Windows Defender Firewall", then "Change settings".
    3. Find every Python entry and tick Private.
    4. Click OK and restart the server.

    #Change the network from Public to Private

    Windows treats a Public network as untrusted and blocks incoming connections on it. Do this on the host laptop.

    Settings > Network & internet > Wi-Fi (or Ethernet) > click the network you are on > Network profile type > Private network.

    List the connections and their profile:

    Get-NetConnectionProfile

    Set one to Private (PowerShell as administrator), using the InterfaceAlias from the list, usually Wi-Fi or Ethernet:

    Set-NetConnectionProfile -InterfaceAlias "<adapter-name>" -NetworkCategory Private

    The other option is to allow the server on Public networks in the firewall prompt or rule. That accepts connections from everyone on that network, so the PIN becomes the only barrier. Prefer Private on a network you trust.

    #School network blocks device-to-device traffic

    Many school and guest Wi-Fi networks use client isolation: every device reaches the internet, but devices cannot reach each other. Live mode cannot work through that.

    Put the team on its own network instead: a phone hotspot or a small travel router. The competition images still need internet to send scores, so the network you pick must have working internet. On a phone hotspot that traffic uses mobile data.

    #Test the connection from a teammate's computer

    Test the port from a teammate's Windows computer (PowerShell), with the host's address in place of <host-ip>. Replace 8080 if the server printed a different port:

    Test-NetConnection <host-ip> -Port 8080

    You should see:

    TcpTestSucceeded : True

    A quick ping also works when the host allows it:

    ping <host-ip>

    Windows blocks incoming ping by default, so a failed ping to a Windows host proves nothing. A failed Test-NetConnection means the firewall, network profile or client isolation is still blocking. If it succeeds, open the address in the browser.

    Also turn off any VPN on the host laptop.

    #The server stopped answering

    Someone probably clicked inside the server window and put it in Select mode, which pauses it. Click the window and press Esc. To stop it happening again, right-click the window's title bar > Properties and untick QuickEdit Mode.

    #Port is already in use

    The server is probably already running in another window. If it is not, start it on another port (for example --port 8090 or -Port 8090) and give teammates the new address.

    #The address changed

    If the host laptop slept or changed networks, its address may have changed. Restart the server and read the new address from the window.

    #Start over or clean up

    To clear everyone's ticks, use Reset team in the sidebar. To clear everything, including chat and notes, stop the server and delete cp-live-state.json from the live folder. If the state file is damaged, the server renames it to cp-live-state.json.bad and starts fresh.

    When you are done with live mode, remove the PowerShell server's firewall rule as shown in option B.

    #Rules and safety

    Live mode stays on your local network and does not use the internet. It only carries your own team's ticks, chat and notes, so it works as a team communication tool.

    The Rules Book also forbids outside assistance and online resources made specifically for CyberPatriot during a round (rules summary). Ask your coach whether live mode is allowed before you use it in a scored round.

    • Never expose the server to the internet (no port forwarding, no tunnels).
    • Never share the PIN with anyone outside the team.

    #If live mode will not work on your network

    Use a shared Google Sheet as the team checklist and a group chat for messages and the change log. The same rules question applies, so check with your coach first.

    Rules that affect how you work

    jump:start-rules

    A summary of the CyberPatriot 19 Rules Book. Before Round 1, open the real Rules Book (uscyberpatriot.org or your coach's dashboard) and confirm anything that matters; the Rules Book wins wherever this summary differs.

    Before you power on the first image

    1. Start only when the whole team is ready. The 4-hour clock starts when the first image powers on.
    2. Run each image on one computer only.
    3. Leave the CyberPatriot folder, the CCS Client and the scoring report shortcut alone.
    4. During the round: no outside help, no AI tools, no online resources made for CyberPatriot.
    5. Read the README before you change anything (first 15 minutes).

    #Time and images

    • Each round runs from Thursday to Sunday. Your team picks one continuous 4-hour period inside that window.
    • The clock starts when the first image is powered on. Opening an image early "just to check" starts your round.
    • Run only one copy of each image at a time. Opening the same image on a second computer, or a second copy on the same computer, triggers a multiple instance penalty.
    • Do not modify, delete or stop anything in the CyberPatriot folder, the scoring service (CCS Client) or the scoring report shortcut.
    • Do not snapshot, clone or copy images unless the round instructions say you may.

    #People and help

    • The roster has 2 to 6 students. At most 5 compete at one time, with one substitution allowed per round.
    • No outside assistance once the round starts. Coaches and mentors may handle logistics and timekeeping but may not give advice.
    • Posting questions on forums or talking with other teams during the round counts as outside assistance.

    #Resources, scripts and AI

    Item What the rules say
    Printed or handwritten notes and checklists Allowed.
    General online documentation (Microsoft Learn, man pages, CIS Benchmarks) Allowed during online rounds.
    Online resources made specifically for CyberPatriot (shared checklists, posted scripts) Prohibited during a round. Publicly posting CyberPatriot resources is also prohibited.
    Scripts your team wrote Allowed in online rounds at your own risk. Banned at the National Finals.
    AI tools during a round (chatbots, AI-generated scripts) Prohibited.
    Paid AI products in connection with the competition Prohibited at any time. Free AI tools are allowed for training outside rounds.
    How this guide and live mode fit the rules

    This guide is an offline file on your own computer, used like printed notes. Keep it that way: do not post it publicly or host it online.

    The scripts in this guide were not written by your team. Read the Rules Book's paragraphs on scripts and AI and decide as a team how you will use them in scored rounds.

    Team live mode stays on your local network and only carries your own team's messages. Ask your coach before using it in a scored round.

    #Scoring rules worth knowing

    • Not every vulnerability is scored. A fix that earns nothing may still be correct.
    • Changes that conflict with the README scenario cost points: deleting an authorized user, stopping a required service, removing required software. Undoing the change returns the points.
    • The score updates every few minutes and only while the image can reach the scoring server (scoring problems).

    Round plan and 4-hour timeline

    jump:start-round

    Round start in order

    1. Give each image one person who makes the changes, and give the Cisco quiz and Packet Tracer to one person.
    2. Power on the images one at a time, enter the Unique Identifier and check the scoring report says connected.
    3. Read each README fully and answer the Forensics Questions before fixing anything (playbook).
    4. Do the basics on every image: users, admins, passwords, password and lockout policy, firewall, updates, antivirus.
    5. Write every change in the change log with the time and the score before and after.

    #What is in each round

    Round Dates Content
    Practice Round Oct 7-20, 2026 Practice images: Windows 11, Windows Server, Linux Mint, Cisco quiz (modules 3-7), Packet Tracer (modules 1-7). Does not count.
    Round 1 (Open and All Service) Oct 22-25, 2026 Windows 11 (100), Linux Mint 21 (100), Cisco networking quiz modules 3-7 (10), Packet Tracer modules 1-7 (20). Total 230.
    Training Round 2 From Oct 30, 2026 Practice with answer keys. Does not count.
    Round 2 Nov 12-15, 2026 Placement round. After it, high school teams are split into Platinum, Gold and Silver tiers.
    State Round Dec 10-13, 2026 Teams compete within their tier. The Cisco portion grows to 100 points per round from here on.
    Semifinals Jan 21-23, 2027 Qualifying teams only.
    National Finals Mar 12-16, 2027 In person.

    Later rounds add Windows Server 2022 and Debian 12 images. Confirm each round's exact images and points in the round instructions.

    The two OS images are worth 200 of the 230 points in Round 1, so most hands belong on the images. The Cisco quiz and Packet Tracer are 30 points together; finish them early and with time to spare.

    #4-hour timeline

    Time Do
    0:00-0:10 Open the images one at a time, enter the Unique Identifier, confirm the scoring report shows the image connected. Everyone reads their image's README fully.
    0:10-0:40 Forensics Questions first on every image, because fixes can destroy evidence. Write down the authorized users and administrators from the README.
    0:40-1:30 High-value basics on every image: users, admins, passwords, password and lockout policy, firewall, updates started, antivirus. These are scored on almost every image.
    1:30-3:00 Services, unwanted software, prohibited files, malware and persistence, security options, application hardening (SSH, FTP, browsers).
    3:00-3:40 Deep pass: registry, sysctl and PAM details. Take a second look at anything that did not score and re-read the README for missed requirements.
    3:40-4:00 Stop making risky changes. Confirm the score is stable, finish any Cisco piece that is left, and record the final score.

    Run the Cisco quiz and Packet Tracer alongside the images. Start them early so a slow website cannot eat the last hour.

    #Work as a team without stepping on each other

    • One person changes each image at a time. When two people change the same image, nobody knows which change scored or which one cost points.
    • Keep a shared change log (paper, a text file on the physical computer, or the Change log channel in live mode): time, image, what you changed, score before and after. When the score drops, the log tells you what to undo.
    • Say score changes out loud. A drop right after a change is the cheapest moment to undo it.
    • Ask before deleting anything the README might care about: users, services, software, files in home folders.
    • Swap images when stuck. If an image has not moved in 30 minutes, trade with someone for a fresh look.
    • Use the one team password everywhere and tell everyone when you set it (team password).

    First 15 minutes on any image

    jump:start-first15

    Before changing anything

    Read the whole README and answer (or at least read) every Forensics Question. Many answers live in files, logs, users or processes that your fixes would remove.

    Fastest high-value order

    Users and admins, passwords, password policy, lockout policy, firewall, automatic updates, antivirus, then services and software. These categories appear on nearly every image.

    PreviousRound plan and 4-hour timelineNextScoring report, penalties and connection problems

    Scoring report, penalties and connection problems

    jump:start-scoring

    Score dropped

    1. Open the scoring report and read the Penalties list.
    2. Find the change in your change log made just before the drop.
    3. Undo that change.
    4. Wait 2-3 minutes and refresh the report to see the points return.

    #Reading the scoring report

    The scoring report is a desktop shortcut that opens in a browser. It shows:

    • total points and the number of vulnerabilities found out of the total
    • each scored item in plain words
    • penalties
    • connection status and the time of the last update

    It updates on its own every few minutes. Refresh the page to see the latest.

    #Score went down

    1. Read the penalties list on the report. It names what was penalized, for example a removed user or a stopped service.
    2. Check the change log for the change made just before the drop and undo it.
    3. Refresh after 2-3 minutes. Undoing the change returns the points.

    Common causes:

    • removing an authorized user
    • taking a user out of Administrators (or sudo) when the README lists them as an admin
    • stopping or removing a required service (SSH, Apache, Samba, FTP, IIS, RDP)
    • uninstalling required software
    • deleting files in a folder the README says is needed
    • breaking a config file so the service crashes

    #Score is not updating

    1. Wait 2-3 minutes and refresh. Updates are not instant.
    2. Check the image has network access (commands below). If you disabled the network adapter, changed DNS or edited the hosts file, undo it.
    3. Check the firewall still allows outbound traffic (commands below). The score cannot upload if outbound is blocked.
    4. Do not restart, reinstall or stop the scoring service. If the report says the image is not connected for more than 10 minutes, tell the coach, who contacts the CyberPatriot Operations Center.

    #Test network access from the image

    ping 8.8.8.8

    Some networks block ping. Test a web connection too (PowerShell):

    Test-NetConnection www.google.com -Port 443

    TcpTestSucceeded : True means the image can reach the internet.

    ping -c 3 8.8.8.8

    Some networks block ping. Test a web connection too:

    wget -q --spider https://www.google.com && echo online

    #Check outbound traffic is allowed

    Show the outbound default for each profile (PowerShell):

    Get-NetFirewallProfile | Select-Object Name, Enabled, DefaultOutboundAction

    Allow or NotConfigured is fine. If any shows Block, run this as administrator:

    Set-NetFirewallProfile -All -DefaultOutboundAction Allow

    sudo ufw status verbose

    The Default line should include allow (outgoing). If it says deny (outgoing) or reject (outgoing):

    sudo ufw default allow outgoing
    PreviousFirst 15 minutes on any imageNextForensics questions playbook (any OS)
    GO

    Forensics questions playbook (any OS)

    jump:start-forensics

    Answer forensics first

    Fixes delete evidence. Answer the Forensics Questions before removing users, files, software or services.

    Fast path

    1. Open the Forensics Question file on the desktop with Notepad (Linux: xed or nano), logged in as the normal desktop user and without sudo.
    2. Read exactly what format the question wants: full path or file name, upper or lower case, one answer or several.
    3. Find the answer with the commands below.
    4. Type it after ANSWER: on the same line and save the file.
    5. Wait a few minutes and refresh the scoring report.

    #How to write the answer

    • Do not change the file name or the question text.
    • Type the answer after ANSWER: on the same line, exactly as asked (case, spacing, full path or file name).
    • If the question wants several answers, put one on each ANSWER: line.
    • A wrong answer does not cost points, so you can change it and try again.

    #Decode hidden text

    #Tell which encoding it is

    Looks like Probably
    Letters A-Z a-z, digits, + and /, often ends with = Base64
    Only 0-9 and a-f, even length Hex
    Groups of 8 zeros and ones Binary
    Real-looking words with the wrong letters ROT13 or another Caesar shift

    The decoder tool in this guide handles these too and tries all 25 Caesar shifts.

    #Decode Base64

    [Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString([Convert]::FromBase64String('<base64-text>'))

    If the result has a gap after every letter, it was UTF-16 text. Swap UTF8 for Unicode and run it again.

    echo '<base64-text>' | base64 -d

    #Decode hex

    -join (('<hex-text>' -replace '[^0-9a-fA-F]','') -split '(..)' | Where-Object {$_} | ForEach-Object {[char][Convert]::ToInt32($_,16)})

    echo '<hex-text>' | xxd -r -p

    If xxd is missing, use Python:

    python3 -c "print(bytes.fromhex('<hex-text>').decode())"

    Both handle hex with or without spaces between the bytes.

    #Decode binary

    -join (('<binary-text>' -replace '[^01]','') -split '(.{8})' | Where-Object {$_} | ForEach-Object {[char][Convert]::ToInt32($_,2)})

    echo '<binary-text>' | perl -lpe '$_=pack("B*",join("",split))'

    Both handle 8-bit groups with or without spaces.

    #Decode ROT13 or another Caesar shift

    ROT13:

    -join ('<encoded-text>'.ToCharArray() | ForEach-Object { $c = [int]$_; if ($c -ge 65 -and $c -le 90) { [char](65 + ($c - 52) % 26) } elseif ($c -ge 97 -and $c -le 122) { [char](97 + ($c - 84) % 26) } else { $_ } })

    All 25 shifts, one per line, numbered by shift:

    1..25 | ForEach-Object { $n = $_; "$n " + -join ('<encoded-text>'.ToCharArray() | ForEach-Object { $c = [int]$_; if ($c -ge 65 -and $c -le 90) { [char](65 + ($c - 65 + $n) % 26) } elseif ($c -ge 97 -and $c -le 122) { [char](97 + ($c - 97 + $n) % 26) } else { $_ } }) }

    ROT13:

    echo '<encoded-text>' | tr 'A-Za-z' 'N-ZA-Mn-za-m'

    All 25 shifts, one per line, numbered by shift:

    python3 -c "import sys,string as s;t=sys.argv[1];[print(n,t.translate(str.maketrans(s.ascii_letters,s.ascii_lowercase[n:]+s.ascii_lowercase[:n]+s.ascii_uppercase[n:]+s.ascii_uppercase[:n]))) for n in range(1,26)]" '<encoded-text>'

    Read down the list and pick the line that is real words.

    #Hashes

    #Hash a file

    Change SHA256 to MD5 or SHA1 as the question asks:

    Get-FileHash '<file>' -Algorithm SHA256

    certutil -hashfile "<file>" MD5

    md5sum '<file>'

    sha1sum '<file>'

    sha256sum '<file>'

    Get-FileHash prints hashes in upper case; certutil and the Linux tools print lower case. Both are the same hash; type it in the case the question asks for.

    #Hash a piece of text

    [BitConverter]::ToString([Security.Cryptography.MD5]::Create().ComputeHash([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes('<plain-text>'))).Replace('-','').ToLower()

    For SHA-256, change MD5 to SHA256.

    The -n stops echo from adding a newline, which would change the hash:

    echo -n '<plain-text>' | md5sum

    #Find the file that has a given hash

    Get-ChildItem C:\Users -Recurse -File -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Get-FileHash -Algorithm MD5 | Where-Object Hash -eq '<hash>' | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Path

    sudo find /home -type f -exec md5sum {} + | grep -i '<hash>'

    Change MD5/md5sum to match the hash type (MD5 is 32 characters, SHA-1 is 40, SHA-256 is 64). Widen the search to C:\ or / if nothing turns up.

    #Find files and text

    #Find a file by name

    Get-ChildItem C:\ -Recurse -Force -Filter '*<file-name>*' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty FullName

    sudo find / -iname '*<file-name>*' 2>/dev/null

    #Find text inside files

    Get-ChildItem C:\Users -Recurse -File -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-String -Pattern '<search-text>' -SimpleMatch -List | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Path

    sudo grep -rIl '<search-text>' /home /etc /var/www 2>/dev/null

    #Find hidden files and alternate data streams

    Hidden files under the user folders:

    Get-ChildItem C:\Users -Recurse -Force -Hidden -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty FullName

    Alternate data streams on one file, then the contents of a stream:

    Get-Item '<file>' -Stream *

    Get-Content '<file>' -Stream '<stream-name>'

    Every file under the user folders that has an extra stream:

    Get-ChildItem C:\Users -Recurse -File -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Get-Item -Stream * -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object Stream -ne ':$DATA' | Select-Object FileName, Stream, Length

    Zone.Identifier streams are normal on downloaded files. Anything else is worth a look.

    Hidden files start with a dot. List them in a folder:

    ls -la '<path>'

    Find hidden files and folders in the usual places:

    sudo find /home /root /tmp /var/tmp -name '.*' 2>/dev/null

    #File details

    #Owner of a file

    (Get-Acl '<file>').Owner

    stat -c '%U' '<file>'

    #Created and modified time

    Get-Item '<file>' | Select-Object CreationTime, LastWriteTime, LastAccessTime

    stat '<file>'

    Modify is the last content change and Birth is the creation time (shown on ext4 with Mint 21).

    #Image metadata and hidden text in images

    Right-click the image > Properties > Details for camera, author, comments and dates.

    Pull readable text out of any file (prints every run of 6 or more printable characters):

    [regex]::Matches([Text.Encoding]::GetEncoding(28591).GetString([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes((Resolve-Path '<file>').Path)), '[\x20-\x7E]{6,}') | ForEach-Object Value

    exiftool is often not installed on Mint. Install it (needs internet), then read every metadata field:

    sudo apt install libimage-exiftool-perl

    exiftool '<file>'

    Pull readable text out of any file:

    strings '<file>' | less

    If strings is missing (it comes with the binutils package), use grep:

    grep -a -o '[[:print:]]\{6,\}' '<file>'

    #Users and groups

    #Groups a user belongs to

    Look at "Local Group Memberships" (add /domain on a domain controller):

    net user <username>

    Members of one group:

    net localgroup <groupname>

    id <username>

    Members of one group:

    getent group <groupname>

    #User ID (SID or UID)

    Get-LocalUser <username> | Select-Object Name, SID

    id -u <username>

    #Recent logins

    The "Last logon" line of net user <username> shows one user's last login. For the full history, read Security events with ID 4624 (PowerShell as administrator):

    Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security'; Id=4624} -MaxEvents 50 | Select-Object TimeCreated, @{n='User';e={$_.Properties[5].Value}}, @{n='LogonType';e={$_.Properties[8].Value}}

    Logon type 2 is at the keyboard, 3 is over the network, 10 is Remote Desktop. In the GUI: Event Viewer > Windows Logs > Security, filter on 4624.

    last

    lastlog

    sudo grep -a 'session opened' /var/log/auth.log | tail -n 20

    #Processes, ports and scheduled jobs

    #Program listening on a port

    TCP:

    Get-Process -Id (Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort <port> -State Listen).OwningProcess

    UDP:

    Get-Process -Id (Get-NetUDPEndpoint -LocalPort <port>).OwningProcess

    The last column is the PID:

    netstat -ano | findstr :<port>

    tasklist /fi "PID eq <pid>"

    sudo ss -tulpn | grep ':<port> '

    #Path and command line of a running process

    Use the full process name including .exe (PowerShell as administrator to see other users' processes):

    Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='<process-name>'" | Select-Object ProcessId, ExecutablePath, CommandLine

    Find the PID, then the program file and its command line:

    pgrep -a <process-name>

    sudo readlink -f /proc/<pid>/exe

    sudo cat /proc/<pid>/cmdline | tr '\0' ' '

    #What a scheduled task or cron job runs

    schtasks /query /tn "<task-name>" /v /fo LIST

    Just the program and its arguments (PowerShell):

    (Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName '<task-name>').Actions | Select-Object Execute, Arguments

    sudo crontab -l -u <username>

    cat /etc/crontab

    ls -la /etc/cron.d /etc/cron.hourly /etc/cron.daily /etc/cron.weekly /etc/cron.monthly

    systemctl list-timers --all

    #Installed software

    #Installed program or package version

    Get-ItemProperty HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*, HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\* | Where-Object DisplayName -like '*<app-name>*' | Select-Object DisplayName, DisplayVersion

    The GUI shows the same list: Settings > Apps > Installed apps.

    dpkg -l | grep -i <package>

    apt policy <package>

    Vulnerability categories mapped to this guide

    jump:start-categories

    The Rules Book groups scored vulnerabilities into general categories, and the score results use similar names. The exact names change a little between seasons. Use the table to find where to look on each image.

    Category What it usually means Windows 11 Server Linux Mint
    Forensics Questions Answer questions in desktop files w11-readme, start-forensics srv-checklist lin-readme
    User Policy / User Auditing Unauthorized users or admins, weak passwords, Guest or root enabled w11-users srv-ad-users lin-users, lin-sudo
    Password Policy Length, complexity, history, age w11-passpol srv-gpo lin-passpol
    Login Policy / Account lockout Lockout threshold, auto-login, last user shown w11-passpol, w11-secopts srv-gpo lin-lockout, lin-login
    Access control and settings / Local Policies Security options, user rights, audit policy w11-secopts, w11-audit srv-gpo lin-kernel, lin-apparmor-audit
    Firewall Firewall off, unneeded open ports w11-firewall w11-firewall lin-firewall
    Insecure Services / Service Auditing Telnet, FTP, Remote Registry and other risky services w11-services srv-services, srv-roles lin-services
    Application Security Hardening the apps the README requires w11-browsers, w11-remote srv-iis, srv-ftp, srv-dns-dhcp lin-ssh, lin-required-services, lin-firefox
    File Sharing and Permissions Open shares, bad permissions w11-shares srv-smb lin-files
    Updates (OS and application) Automatic updates off, outdated apps w11-updates srv-updates-defender lin-updates
    Antivirus / Defensive Countermeasures Defender off, exclusions added w11-defender srv-updates-defender lin-apparmor-audit
    Malware / Unwanted Software Hacking tools, backdoors, persistence w11-software, w11-malware srv-scripts lin-software, lin-malware
    Prohibited Files / Policy Violation Media files, password lists, files or services the company does not allow w11-files w11-files lin-files
    Miscellaneous / Operating System Settings Registry, sysctl, UAC and other settings w11-registry, w11-uac-misc srv-ad-hardening lin-kernel

    Windows 11 master checklist

    jump:w11-checklist

    Work top to bottom and tick items as you go; the boxes are shared live with the team. Items that depend on the README say so. Log every change (what, where, old value) so you can undo it.

    README and Forensics Questions first

    Read the whole README and answer the Forensics Questions before you delete users, files or software. A fix can destroy the evidence a question asks about. Never touch the CyberPatriot folder, the CCS Client or the scoring report.

    #First 10 minutes

    #Users and groups

    #Password and lockout policy

    #Audit policy

    #Security options and user rights

    #Firewall

    #Defender

    #Updates

    #Services

    #Optional features

    #Shares and remote access

    #Software and files

    #Malware and persistence

    #Final pass

    PreviousVulnerability categories mapped to this guideNextREADME and forensics questions first
    W11

    README and forensics questions first

    jump:w11-readme

    Never touch the scoring engine

    Do not stop, delete, disable or firewall anything named CyberPatriot, CCS or CCS Client. Do not delete the README, the scoring report or the forensics files. Breaking scoring can cost you the whole image.

    Fast path

    1. Open the CyberPatriot README shortcut on the desktop and read all of it, including the bottom of the page.
    2. Copy the authorized users, authorized administrators, required services and required software into your team notes.
    3. Open each Forensics Question N.txt on the desktop in Notepad and answer what you can before changing anything (how).
    4. Open the CyberPatriot Scoring Report shortcut and confirm it shows a score.
    5. Start a change log (format), then harden in checklist order.

    #Where things are on a Windows 11 image

    Item Location Notes
    README Desktop shortcut "CyberPatriot README" Opens a web page. Read every line, including the bottom.
    Forensics Questions Desktop: Forensics Question 1.txt, Forensics Question 2.txt, ... Plain text. Open with Notepad.
    Scoring Report Desktop shortcut "CyberPatriot Scoring Report" Refreshes every minute or two and needs internet.
    CyberPatriot folder C:\CyberPatriot and the CCS Client scoring service Never modify, move or delete.

    #Answer a forensics question

    1. Right-click the file > Open with > Notepad.
    2. Read the question and the example answer format.
    3. Type your answer after ANSWER: on the answer line, for example ANSWER: C:\Users\Public\notes.txt.
    4. Press Ctrl+S. Do not rename the file, change its encoding or delete the other lines.
    5. Check the scoring report a minute later.

    You can also open a question from PowerShell:

    notepad "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\Forensics Question 1.txt"

    Match the example format exactly

    Copy the case, path style and separators from the example. Add quotes only if the example has them. If the file has several ANSWER: lines, put one answer on each.

    #Forensics commands

    Run these in PowerShell. Most work without admin rights; reading other users' files needs an elevated window.

    #Find a user's SID

    Get-LocalUser -Name <username> | Select-Object Name, SID

    For the account you are signed in as:

    whoami /user

    #Hash a file

    SHA256 is the default. Change -Algorithm to MD5 or SHA1 if the question asks for those.

    Get-FileHash -Path "<path>" -Algorithm SHA256

    certutil -hashfile "<path>" SHA256

    #Decode Base64 text

    [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString([System.Convert]::FromBase64String('<base64-text>'))

    Save the Base64 text in in.txt first, then decode it into out.txt and print it:

    certutil -decode in.txt out.txt
type out.txt

    ROT13, Caesar and other simple ciphers

    Use CyberChef (gchq.github.io/CyberChef) in the browser if the image has internet. It runs locally in the page.

    #Find a file by name

    Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue -Filter "*<part-of-name>*"

    #Find which file contains some text

    Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users -Recurse -Force -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-String -Pattern "<search-text>" -List | Select-Object Path

    #See a user's groups or a group's members

    net user <username>

    net localgroup "<groupname>"

    #Find the process that owns a listening port

    Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort <port> -State Listen | ForEach-Object { Get-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess }

    #Read hidden alternate data streams

    List the streams on a file, then read one by name:

    Get-Item "<path>" -Stream *

    Get-Content "<path>" -Stream <stream-name>

    A normal file shows only :$DATA. Any other stream name is hidden data.

    #Check file times and owner

    Get-Item "<path>" | Select-Object FullName, CreationTime, LastWriteTime
(Get-Acl "<path>").Owner

    #Keep a change log

    Keep notes in a file away from the desktop forensics files (for example Documents\changes.txt) or on paper. For each change, write the time, what you changed, the old value, the new value and the score before and after. When the score drops, the log tells you what to undo.

    10:14  Removed user "<username>" from Administrators     score 12 -> 15
10:20  Disabled service RemoteRegistry (was Manual)       score 15 -> 17
10:31  Disabled Print Spooler (was Automatic)             score 17 -> 15  UNDO (README requires printing)

    Check it worked

    Each correct forensics answer appears as a scored item on the scoring report within a few minutes. If it does not, re-read the example format.

    Why forensics come first, and how penalties work

    Forensics questions often ask about the exact user, file, program, port or setting you are about to remove. Answer every question that mentions one of those before you remove it. The read-only recon script in w11-scripts records the original state so you can still answer later questions.

    The scoring report shows penalties when you remove a required user, service or program. Undo the change and the points come back. Not every vulnerability is scored, so a fix that adds nothing is not proof it was wrong.

    PreviousWindows 11 master checklistNextUsers and groups
    W11

    Users and groups

    jump:w11-users

    The README defines who is allowed

    Never delete or demote a user the README lists as authorized, and never delete your own account. Answer forensics questions about users first.

    Fast path

    1. Open PowerShell as administrator (Start, type powershell, Run as administrator).

    2. List local users and administrators:

      Get-LocalUser | Select-Object Name, Enabled
net localgroup Administrators

    3. Delete every user the README does not list (how).

    4. Remove every administrator the README does not list as an admin (how).

    5. Disable Guest:

      Disable-LocalUser -Name Guest

    6. Set the team password on every other account (how).

    7. Check the other privileged groups (table).

    #Open the Local Users and Groups console

    • Win+R > lusrmgr.msc > Users or Groups. Home edition does not have it; use Settings or the commands below.
    • Win+R > compmgmt.msc > System Tools > Local Users and Groups opens the same view.
    • Settings > Accounts > Other users can add or remove accounts and switch a user between Administrator and Standard User.
    • Win+R > netplwiz lists users with their group.

    #List users and administrators

    Get-LocalUser | Select-Object Name, Enabled, PasswordRequired, PasswordExpires, PasswordLastSet, LastLogon, Description | Format-Table -AutoSize

    Get-LocalGroupMember -Group Administrators | Select-Object Name, ObjectClass, PrincipalSource

    net user
net localgroup Administrators

    Administrator, Guest, DefaultAccount and WDAGUtilityAccount are built in. Every other name must appear in the README.

    net user hides names ending in $

    Use Get-LocalUser for the final check. See names ending in $.

    #Compare the README with the system in one paste

    Edit the first two lines before pasting into elevated PowerShell. $authUsers holds every authorized user from the README, including admins and yourself. $authAdmins holds the authorized administrators, including yourself. Spell names exactly as the README does.

    $authUsers  = @('<user1>','<user2>','<user3>')
$authAdmins = @('<admin1>','<admin2>')
$builtin    = @('Administrator','Guest','DefaultAccount','WDAGUtilityAccount')

"--- Users NOT in README (candidates to delete) ---"
Get-LocalUser | Where-Object { $_.Name -notin $authUsers -and $_.Name -notin $builtin } | Select-Object Name, Enabled

"--- README users that do NOT exist (create them) ---"
$authUsers | Where-Object { -not (Get-LocalUser -Name $_ -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) }

"--- Admins NOT authorized (remove from Administrators) ---"
net localgroup Administrators | Select-Object -Skip 6 | Where-Object { $_ -and $_ -notmatch 'command completed' } |
  Where-Object { ($_ -split '\\')[-1].Trim() -notin $authAdmins -and ($_ -split '\\')[-1].Trim() -ne 'Administrator' }

"--- Authorized admins missing from Administrators ---"
$current = net localgroup Administrators | Select-Object -Skip 6 | ForEach-Object { ($_ -split '\\')[-1].Trim() }
$authAdmins | Where-Object { $_ -notin $current }

    Each heading line prints, followed by the names that need action. An empty list under a heading means nothing to fix.

    Why the script uses net localgroup

    Get-LocalGroupMember stops with an error if the group contains an orphaned SID from a deleted account. net localgroup always works.

    #Remove an unauthorized user

    Remove-LocalUser -Name <username>

    net user <username> /delete

    lusrmgr.msc > Users > right-click the user > Delete > Yes.

    You should see no output from PowerShell, or "The command completed successfully." from cmd. The user's profile folder in C:\Users stays behind; leave it until forensics questions are answered.

    Verify

    Get-LocalUser -Name <username> returns "User was not found."

    #Demote an unauthorized administrator

    Remove-LocalGroupMember -Group Administrators -Member <username>

    net localgroup Administrators <username> /delete

    Settings > Accounts > Other users > the user > Change account type > Standard User.

    A demoted user should still be in Users. Add them back; the error "already a member" is fine:

    net localgroup Users <username> /add

    #Promote a README administrator

    Add-LocalGroupMember -Group Administrators -Member <username>

    net localgroup Administrators <username> /add

    #Create a missing user

    $pw = ConvertTo-SecureString '<team-password>' -AsPlainText -Force
New-LocalUser -Name <username> -Password $pw -FullName "<username>"
Add-LocalGroupMember -Group Users -Member <username>

    net user <username> <team-password> /add

    net user /add puts the new account in Users automatically. If Add-LocalGroupMember says the user is already a member, that is fine.

    #Create a group and add members

    New-LocalGroup -Name <groupname>
Add-LocalGroupMember -Group <groupname> -Member <user1>,<user2>

    net localgroup <groupname> /add
net localgroup <groupname> <username> /add

    Verify

    net localgroup <groupname> lists exactly the members the README asked for.

    #Disable the Guest account

    Disable-LocalUser -Name Guest

    net user Guest /active:no

    The matching policy is secpol.msc > Local Policies > Security Options > Accounts: Guest account status = Disabled. Both change the same setting.

    #Disable the built-in Administrator account

    Run whoami first. If you are signed in as the built-in Administrator, do not disable it until another admin account with a known password works.

    Disable-LocalUser -Name Administrator

    net user Administrator /active:no

    #Leave DefaultAccount and WDAGUtilityAccount disabled

    Both are built-in, system-managed accounts that are disabled by default. Do not delete them. If either shows Enabled, disable it:

    Disable-LocalUser -Name DefaultAccount

    WDAGUtilityAccount belongs to Microsoft Defender Application Guard and may not exist on newer builds.

    #Set a strong password on every account

    Use one strong team password (example Cyb3rP@tri0t!2026) for every account except your own, unless the README says otherwise.

    List the accounts to change, then run:

    $pw = ConvertTo-SecureString '<team-password>' -AsPlainText -Force
foreach ($u in @('<user1>','<user2>','<user3>')) { Set-LocalUser -Name $u -Password $pw }

    net user <username> <team-password>

    lusrmgr.msc > Users > right-click the user > Set Password > Proceed.

    Do not change your own password casually

    If you change the password of the account you are signed in as and forget it, you are locked out. If the README tells you to change it, write the new one down first.

    #Fix password never expires and password not required

    #Find the accounts

    Enabled accounts whose password never expires:

    Get-LocalUser | Where-Object { $_.Enabled -and $_.PasswordExpires -eq $null } | Select-Object Name

    Enabled accounts that do not require a password:

    Get-LocalUser | Where-Object { $_.Enabled -and -not $_.PasswordRequired } | Select-Object Name

    #Fix one account

    Set-LocalUser -Name <username> -PasswordNeverExpires $false -UserMayChangePassword $true

    Set-LocalUser has no switch for Password not required, so clear that one with net user in the same window:

    net user <username> /passwordreq:yes

    net user <username> /passwordreq:yes
net user <username> /passwordchg:yes

    lusrmgr.msc > Users > double-click the user > clear "Password never expires" and "User cannot change password" > OK.

    /passwordchg:yes allows the user to change their own password. To force a new password at next sign-in for another user (never yourself), run net user <username> /logonpasswordchg:yes.

    PasswordExpires still empty after the fix

    PasswordExpires shows a date only after a maximum password age is set. Set it in w11-passpol, then check again.

    #Find hidden users

    #Users hidden from the sign-in screen

    reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\SpecialAccounts\UserList"

    Each value name is a username. A DWORD of 0 hides that user from the sign-in screen, but the account still exists. If the user is unauthorized, delete the account, then delete the value:

    reg delete "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\SpecialAccounts\UserList" /v <username> /f

    "ERROR: The system was unable to find the specified registry key or value" means nothing is hidden there.

    #Account names ending in $

    net user does not list accounts whose names end in $. Get-LocalUser and lusrmgr.msc do:

    Get-LocalUser | Where-Object Name -like '*$'

    #Check privileged groups

    Run net localgroup "<groupname>" for each group. Members should match what the README implies.

    Group Why it matters Expected members
    Administrators Full control README admins only, plus the built-in Administrator (disabled)
    Remote Desktop Users Can sign in over RDP Empty unless the README names RDP users
    Backup Operators Can read any file through the backup privilege Empty
    Remote Management Users WinRM and PowerShell remoting Empty
    Hyper-V Administrators Control virtual machines Empty
    Network Configuration Operators Change network settings Empty
    Event Log Readers Read event logs Empty
    Power Users Legacy group, near-admin on old systems Empty
    Cryptographic Operators, Distributed COM Users, Performance Log Users, Access Control Assistance Operators, Device Owners Extra privileges Empty
    Guests Guest access Guest only
    Users Normal users Authorized users, NT AUTHORITY\Authenticated Users, NT AUTHORITY\INTERACTIVE

    List every group with its members in one go:

    Get-LocalGroup | ForEach-Object {
  $m = net localgroup "$($_.Name)" | Select-Object -Skip 6 | Where-Object { $_ -and $_ -notmatch 'command completed' }
  "{0,-40} {1}" -f $_.Name, ($m -join ', ')
}

    Remove an extra member with net localgroup "<groupname>" <username> /delete.

    #Rename an account only when asked

    Rename-LocalUser -Name <username> -NewName <new-name>

    Renaming the built-in Administrator or Guest is also a Security Option (w11-secopts). Do it only if the README does not refer to those names; disabling them is what usually scores.

    Verify

    Run the compare script again. Every list under the headings should be empty.

    PreviousREADME and forensics questions firstNextPassword and lockout policy
    W11

    Password and lockout policy

    jump:w11-passpol

    Fast path

    1. Open cmd or PowerShell as administrator.

    2. Set the password policy:

      net accounts /uniquepw:24 /maxpwage:60 /minpwage:1 /minpwlen:12

    3. Set the lockout threshold first:

      net accounts /lockoutthreshold:5

    4. Set the duration, then the reset window, as two separate commands (why the order matters):

      net accounts /lockoutduration:30
net accounts /lockoutwindow:30

    5. Win+R > secpol.msc > Account Policies > Password Policy: set Password must meet complexity requirements = Enabled and Store passwords using reversible encryption = Disabled.

    6. Run net accounts and compare with the expected output.

    #Recommended values

    Setting (secpol name) Value net accounts switch
    Enforce password history 24 passwords remembered /uniquepw:24
    Maximum password age 60 days (30 to 90 is fine) /maxpwage:60
    Minimum password age 1 day /minpwage:1
    Minimum password length 12 (10 to 14 is fine) /minpwlen:12
    Password must meet complexity requirements Enabled none, use secpol or secedit
    Store passwords using reversible encryption Disabled none, use secpol or secedit
    Relax minimum password length limits Not Defined, unless you need a length over 14 none
    Account lockout threshold 5 invalid attempts (5 to 10 is fine) /lockoutthreshold:5
    Account lockout duration 30 minutes /lockoutduration:30
    Reset account lockout counter after 30 minutes /lockoutwindow:30
    Allow Administrator account lockout Enabled none, use secpol

    #Set the password policy

    net accounts /uniquepw:24 /maxpwage:60 /minpwage:1 /minpwlen:12

    You should see "The command completed successfully." net accounts cannot set complexity or reversible encryption; do those next.

    1. Win+R > secpol.msc.
    2. Account Policies > Password Policy.
    3. Double-click each setting and enter the value from the table.

    #Turn on complexity and turn off reversible encryption

    1. Win+R > secpol.msc > Account Policies > Password Policy.
    2. Password must meet complexity requirements > Enabled > OK.
    3. Store passwords using reversible encryption > Disabled > OK.

    Use this on Home edition, which has no secpol.msc. See set everything with secedit.

    #Set the lockout policy

    Set the threshold first:

    net accounts /lockoutthreshold:5

    Then the duration, then the reset window:

    net accounts /lockoutduration:30
net accounts /lockoutwindow:30
    1. secpol.msc > Account Policies > Account Lockout Policy.
    2. Account lockout threshold > 5 > OK. Windows offers suggested values for the other two; accept them.
    3. Account lockout duration > 30 > OK.
    4. Reset account lockout counter after > 30 > OK.
    5. Allow Administrator account lockout > Enabled, if it is listed.

    The rule Windows enforces: Reset account lockout counter after (/lockoutwindow) must be less than or equal to Account lockout duration (/lockoutduration). When you raise both values, set the duration first. When you lower both, set the window first.

    #If net accounts says "The parameter is incorrect"

    The new value broke the window-at-most-duration rule. Run the two commands in the other order. For example, going from 60/60 down to 30/30:

    net accounts /lockoutwindow:30
net accounts /lockoutduration:30

    Duration 0 locks accounts until an admin unlocks them

    /lockoutduration:0 means a locked account stays locked forever. Use 30.

    Windows 11 already ships with a lockout policy

    Clean installs of Windows 11 22H2 and later default to threshold 10, duration 10 minutes, reset 10 minutes and Allow Administrator account lockout Enabled. Upgraded images may still show threshold Never. Either way, set the values above.

    #Set everything with secedit

    secedit works on every edition, including Home, and sets complexity and reversible encryption, which net accounts cannot. The steps:

    1. Export the current policy as a backup.
    2. Write a small template with only the settings to change.
    3. Apply it with secedit /configure.
    4. Check the result with net accounts.

    Run each block in elevated PowerShell. Back up first:

    secedit /export /cfg "$env:USERPROFILE\Documents\secpol-backup.inf" /areas SECURITYPOLICY

    Write the template:

    $inf = "$env:TEMP\passpol.inf"
@'
[Unicode]
Unicode=yes
[System Access]
MinimumPasswordAge = 1
MaximumPasswordAge = 60
MinimumPasswordLength = 12
PasswordComplexity = 1
PasswordHistorySize = 24
ClearTextPassword = 0
LockoutBadCount = 5
ResetLockoutCount = 30
LockoutDuration = 30
[Version]
signature="$CHICAGO$"
Revision=1
'@ | Set-Content -Path $inf -Encoding Unicode

    Apply it:

    secedit /configure /db "$env:TEMP\passpol.sdb" /cfg "$env:TEMP\passpol.inf" /areas SECURITYPOLICY

    You should see "The task has completed successfully." A message that warnings occurred for some attributes is normal. If the lockout duration or window did not change, set them with net accounts.

    #Edit an export by hand

    1. Export: secedit /export /cfg C:\secpol.inf /areas SECURITYPOLICY
    2. Open it: notepad C:\secpol.inf
    3. Under [System Access], change the values to match the table and save. Keep the file's encoding.

    4. Apply it in elevated cmd:

      secedit /configure /db %TEMP%\secpol.sdb /cfg C:\secpol.inf /areas SECURITYPOLICY

    Missing lockout lines in the export

    When LockoutBadCount = 0, secpol shows lockout duration and reset as Not Applicable and the export may not contain LockoutDuration or ResetLockoutCount lines at all, so a find-and-replace has nothing to change. Type the two lines in yourself under [System Access], or set them with net accounts after the threshold.

    #Verify the policy

    net accounts

    Expected output:

    Force user logoff how long after time expires?:       Never
Minimum password age (days):                          1
Maximum password age (days):                          60
Minimum password length:                              12
Length of password history maintained:                24
Lockout threshold:                                    5
Lockout duration (minutes):                           30
Lockout observation window (minutes):                 30
Computer role:                                        WORKSTATION
The command completed successfully.

    net accounts does not show complexity. Check it from an export:

    secedit /export /cfg "$env:TEMP\check.inf" /areas SECURITYPOLICY | Out-Null
Select-String -Path "$env:TEMP\check.inf" -Pattern 'Password|Lockout|ClearText'

    Verify

    net accounts matches the output above and the export shows PasswordComplexity = 1 and ClearTextPassword = 0.

    Existing passwords are not rechecked

    The policy applies at each user's next password change. After setting it, set every other user's password (w11-users) so all accounts comply.

    Minimum length over 14

    secpol.msc and net accounts accept at most 14. To go higher, first enable Password Policy > Relax minimum password length limits; the field then accepts up to 128. Scoring does not need more than 12 to 14. The team password Cyb3rP@tri0t!2026 has 17 characters, so any value up to 14 is safe.

    PreviousUsers and groupsNextAudit policy
    W11

    Audit policy

    jump:w11-audit

    Fast path

    1. Open cmd or PowerShell as administrator.

    2. Turn on success and failure auditing for every subcategory:

      auditpol /set /category:* /success:enable /failure:enable

    3. In secpol.msc > Local Policies > Audit Policy, set all nine entries to Success and Failure (how).

    4. Make subcategory settings win over categories:

      reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v SCENoApplyLegacyAuditPolicy /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f

    5. Check the result with auditpol /get /category:*.

    #Turn on all auditing with auditpol

    Run in elevated cmd or PowerShell:

    auditpol /set /category:* /success:enable /failure:enable

    You should see "The command was successfully executed." "Error 0x00000522" means the window is not elevated.

    #Set the legacy audit policy

    Some images score the classic setting names in secpol.msc, so set them as well.

    secpol.msc > Local Policies > Audit Policy > double-click each of the nine policies > check Success and Failure > OK.

    Legacy policy Value
    Audit account logon events Success, Failure
    Audit account management Success, Failure
    Audit directory service access Success, Failure
    Audit logon events Success, Failure
    Audit object access Success, Failure
    Audit policy change Success, Failure
    Audit privilege use Success, Failure
    Audit process tracking Success, Failure
    Audit system events Success, Failure

    Works on Home edition. In the template, 3 means Success and Failure (1 Success, 2 Failure, 0 no auditing). Write it:

    $inf = "$env:TEMP\audit.inf"
@'
[Unicode]
Unicode=yes
[Event Audit]
AuditSystemEvents = 3
AuditLogonEvents = 3
AuditObjectAccess = 3
AuditPrivilegeUse = 3
AuditPolicyChange = 3
AuditAccountManage = 3
AuditProcessTracking = 3
AuditDSAccess = 3
AuditAccountLogon = 3
[Version]
signature="$CHICAGO$"
Revision=1
'@ | Set-Content -Path $inf -Encoding Unicode

    Apply it, then run auditpol again so every subcategory ends up enabled whichever applied last:

    secedit /configure /db "$env:TEMP\audit.sdb" /cfg "$env:TEMP\audit.inf" /areas SECURITYPOLICY
auditpol /set /category:* /success:enable /failure:enable

    #Turn on auditing for chosen categories

    Use these if you want fewer events than /category:* gives. Category names need quotes when they contain spaces or a slash:

    auditpol /set /category:"Account Logon" /success:enable /failure:enable
auditpol /set /category:"Account Management" /success:enable /failure:enable
auditpol /set /category:"Logon/Logoff" /success:enable /failure:enable
auditpol /set /category:"Policy Change" /success:enable /failure:enable
auditpol /set /category:"Privilege Use" /success:enable /failure:enable
auditpol /set /category:"System" /success:enable /failure:enable
auditpol /set /category:"Detailed Tracking" /success:enable /failure:enable
auditpol /set /category:"Object Access" /success:enable /failure:enable
auditpol /set /category:"DS Access" /success:enable /failure:enable

    One subcategory at a time, for example Credential Validation and Logon:

    auditpol /set /subcategory:"Credential Validation" /success:enable /failure:enable
auditpol /set /subcategory:"Logon" /success:enable /failure:enable

    List every subcategory name with auditpol /list /subcategory:*.

    #Set advanced audit policy in secpol

    secpol.msc > Advanced Audit Policy Configuration > System Audit Policies - Local Group Policy Object > each category > each subcategory > check Configure the following audit events, Success and Failure > OK.

    This writes the same subcategory settings as auditpol, stored in the local policy.

    #Make subcategories override categories

    secpol.msc > Local Policies > Security Options > Audit: Force audit policy subcategory settings (Windows Vista or later) to override audit policy category settings > Enabled.

    reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v SCENoApplyLegacyAuditPolicy /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f

    #Verify auditing

    auditpol /get /category:*

    Every subcategory line should end in "Success and Failure". This filter prints only the lines that do not, so empty output means you are done:

    auditpol /get /category:* | Where-Object { $_ -match '(No Auditing|Success|Failure)\s*$' -and $_ -notmatch 'Success and Failure' }

    Verify

    auditpol /get /category:* shows Success and Failure on every line, and secpol.msc > Local Policies > Audit Policy shows Success, Failure for all nine entries.

    Raise the Security log size

    Optional. A bigger Security log keeps events from being overwritten. Set it to about 192 MB in elevated cmd with wevtutil sl Security /ms:201326592, and check with wevtutil gl Security.

    PreviousPassword and lockout policyNextSecurity options and user rights
    W11

    Security options and user rights

    jump:w11-secopts

    Fast path

    1. Win+R > secpol.msc > Local Policies > Security Options.
    2. Set each policy in the commonly scored table, or paste the reg add blocks into elevated cmd.
    3. Set the UAC options.
    4. Open Local Policies > User Rights Assignment and remove single users and Everyone from powerful rights (how).

    5. Apply policy now:

      gpupdate /force

    6. Close and reopen secpol.msc and confirm the values.

    Double-click a policy, change it, click OK. Most settings apply at once.

    Home edition

    Home has no secpol.msc. Use the reg add blocks and the secedit method.

    #Commonly scored security options

    Registry paths are under HKLM.

    Policy (exact secpol name) Set to Registry equivalent
    Accounts: Administrator account status Disabled, if you have another admin use net user Administrator /active:no
    Accounts: Guest account status Disabled use net user Guest /active:no
    Accounts: Limit local account use of blank passwords to console logon only Enabled SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa LimitBlankPasswordUse = 1
    Accounts: Rename administrator account A non-default name (optional) secpol or secedit only
    Accounts: Rename guest account A non-default name (optional) secpol or secedit only
    Audit: Force audit policy subcategory settings (Windows Vista or later) to override audit policy category settings Enabled SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa SCENoApplyLegacyAuditPolicy = 1
    Audit: Shut down system immediately if unable to log security audits Disabled (leave it) SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa CrashOnAuditFail = 0
    Devices: Prevent users from installing printer drivers Enabled SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print\Providers\LanMan Print Services\Servers AddPrinterDrivers = 1
    Interactive logon: Do not require CTRL+ALT+DEL Disabled SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System DisableCAD = 0
    Interactive logon: Don't display last signed-in (older name: Do not display last user name) Enabled SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System DontDisplayLastUserName = 1
    Interactive logon: Machine inactivity limit 900 seconds SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System InactivityTimeoutSecs = 900
    Interactive logon: Prompt user to change password before expiration 14 days SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon PasswordExpiryWarning = 14
    Interactive logon: Number of previous logons to cache (in case domain controller is not available) 4 or fewer SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon CachedLogonsCount = "4" (REG_SZ)
    Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (always) Enabled SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanWorkstation\Parameters RequireSecuritySignature = 1
    Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (if server agrees) Enabled ...\LanmanWorkstation\Parameters EnableSecuritySignature = 1
    Microsoft network client: Send unencrypted password to third-party SMB servers Disabled ...\LanmanWorkstation\Parameters EnablePlainTextPassword = 0
    Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always) Enabled SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\Parameters RequireSecuritySignature = 1
    Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (if client agrees) Enabled ...\LanmanServer\Parameters EnableSecuritySignature = 1
    Microsoft network server: Disconnect clients when logon hours expire Enabled ...\LanmanServer\Parameters EnableForcedLogOff = 1
    Network access: Allow anonymous SID/Name translation Disabled secpol or secedit only: LSAAnonymousNameLookup = 0
    Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts Enabled SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa RestrictAnonymousSAM = 1
    Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares Enabled SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa RestrictAnonymous = 1
    Network access: Do not allow storage of passwords and credentials for network authentication Enabled SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa DisableDomainCreds = 1
    Network access: Let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users Disabled SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa EveryoneIncludesAnonymous = 0
    Network access: Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares Enabled SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\Parameters RestrictNullSessAccess = 1
    Network access: Shares that can be accessed anonymously Empty ...\LanmanServer\Parameters NullSessionShares = empty REG_MULTI_SZ
    Network access: Named Pipes that can be accessed anonymously Empty ...\LanmanServer\Parameters NullSessionPipes = empty REG_MULTI_SZ
    Network access: Sharing and security model for local accounts Classic - local users authenticate as themselves SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa ForceGuest = 0
    Network security: Allow LocalSystem NULL session fallback Disabled SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 AllowNullSessionFallback = 0
    Network security: Do not store LAN Manager hash value on next password change Enabled SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa NoLMHash = 1
    Network security: Force logoff when logon hours expire Enabled secpol or secedit only: ForceLogoffWhenHourExpire = 1
    Network security: LAN Manager authentication level Send NTLMv2 response only. Refuse LM & NTLM SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa LmCompatibilityLevel = 5
    Network security: LDAP client signing requirements Negotiate signing SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LDAP LDAPClientIntegrity = 1
    Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) clients Require NTLMv2 session security, Require 128-bit encryption SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 NTLMMinClientSec = 537395200
    Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP based (including secure RPC) servers Require NTLMv2 session security, Require 128-bit encryption SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 NTLMMinServerSec = 537395200
    Recovery console: Allow automatic administrative logon Disabled SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Setup\RecoveryConsole SecurityLevel = 0
    Shutdown: Allow system to be shut down without having to log on Disabled SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System ShutdownWithoutLogon = 0
    Shutdown: Clear virtual memory pagefile Enabled (optional, slows shutdown) SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management ClearPageFileAtShutdown = 1
    System objects: Strengthen default permissions of internal system objects (e.g. Symbolic Links) Enabled SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager ProtectionMode = 1

    Leave these alone

    Keep "Audit: Shut down system immediately if unable to log security audits" Disabled; enabling it can crash the image when the log fills. Keep "User Account Control: Only elevate executables that are signed and validated" Disabled; enabling it breaks many programs.

    #User Account Control options

    All are in secpol.msc > Local Policies > Security Options. Registry values are under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System.

    Policy Set to Registry value
    User Account Control: Admin Approval Mode for the Built-in Administrator account Enabled FilterAdministratorToken = 1
    User Account Control: Allow UIAccess applications to prompt for elevation without using the secure desktop Disabled EnableUIADesktopToggle = 0
    User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for administrators in Admin Approval Mode Prompt for consent on the secure desktop (or Prompt for credentials on the secure desktop) ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin = 2 (credentials = 1)
    User Account Control: Behavior of the elevation prompt for standard users Prompt for credentials on the secure desktop ConsentPromptBehaviorUser = 1
    User Account Control: Detect application installations and prompt for elevation Enabled EnableInstallerDetection = 1
    User Account Control: Only elevate UIAccess applications that are installed in secure locations Enabled EnableSecureUIAPaths = 1
    User Account Control: Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode Enabled EnableLUA = 1
    User Account Control: Switch to the secure desktop when prompting for elevation Enabled PromptOnSecureDesktop = 1
    User Account Control: Virtualize file and registry write failures to per-user locations Enabled EnableVirtualization = 1

    EnableLUA needs a restart

    Run all administrators in Admin Approval Mode (EnableLUA) changes only after a restart. Never set it to Disabled.

    #Apply security options with reg add

    Run in elevated cmd. Each line stands alone, so a failed line does not stop the others. Each prints "The operation completed successfully."

    Blank passwords, anonymous access, LM hashes and NTLM level:

    reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v LimitBlankPasswordUse /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v RestrictAnonymousSAM /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v RestrictAnonymous /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v EveryoneIncludesAnonymous /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v NoLMHash /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v LmCompatibilityLevel /t REG_DWORD /d 5 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v DisableDomainCreds /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v SCENoApplyLegacyAuditPolicy /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\Parameters" /v RestrictNullSessAccess /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f

    Sign-in screen, inactivity lock and shutdown without logon:

    reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v DisableCAD /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v DontDisplayLastUserName /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v InactivityTimeoutSecs /t REG_DWORD /d 900 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v ShutdownWithoutLogon /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

    User Account Control:

    reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v EnableLUA /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin /t REG_DWORD /d 2 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v ConsentPromptBehaviorUser /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
