    Turn off double escaping server-wide:

    Set-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Filter 'system.webServer/security/requestFiltering' -Name allowDoubleEscaping -Value $false

    #Hide the Server and X-Powered-By headers

    IIS 10 on Server 2022 can drop the Server header. The second line removes the X-Powered-By custom header:

    Set-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Filter 'system.webServer/security/requestFiltering' -Name removeServerHeader -Value $true
Remove-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Filter 'system.webServer/httpProtocol/customHeaders' -Name '.' -AtElement @{name='X-Powered-By'}

    GUI for X-Powered-By: inetmgr > server node > HTTP Response Headers > X-Powered-By > Remove. Low priority and rarely scored.

    #Turn on logging

    GUI: inetmgr > server node (or site) > Logging > Actions: Enable. Use format W3C and directory %SystemDrive%\inetpub\logs\LogFiles.

    Get-ItemProperty "IIS:\Sites\<site-name>" -Name logFile | Select-Object enabled,directory,logFormat
Set-ItemProperty "IIS:\Sites\<site-name>" -Name logFile.enabled -Value $true

    #Turn off debug and detailed errors in web.config

    Each site's web.config should contain these values (merge them into the existing system.web and system.webServer elements):

    <system.web>
  <compilation debug="false" />
  <customErrors mode="RemoteOnly" />
</system.web>
<system.webServer>
  <httpErrors errorMode="DetailedLocalError" />
  <directoryBrowse enabled="false" />
</system.webServer>

    GUI: inetmgr > site > Error Pages > Edit Feature Settings > Detailed errors for local requests and custom error pages for remote requests.

    While you are in web.config, look for connection strings with plaintext passwords (a likely Forensics answer) and handlers that map odd extensions to script engines.

    #Remove WebDAV

    Uninstall-WindowsFeature Web-DAV-Publishing

    Get-WindowsFeature Web-DAV-Publishing should then show Available. If the README needs WebDAV, inetmgr > site > WebDAV Authoring Rules should have no rule for All users or anonymous users.

    #Fix permissions on C:\inetpub\wwwroot

    icacls C:\inetpub\wwwroot

    Only Administrators, SYSTEM and TrustedInstaller should have write (W, M or F). Users, IIS_IUSRS and IUSR should have read and execute (RX) at most. Remove bad explicit grants and give IIS_IUSRS read back:

    icacls C:\inetpub\wwwroot /remove:g Everyone /T
icacls C:\inetpub\wwwroot /remove:g "IIS_IUSRS" /T
icacls C:\inetpub\wwwroot /grant "IIS_IUSRS:(OI)(CI)RX"

    /remove:g removes only explicit grants. If the bad entry is inherited (shown with (I)), fix it on the parent folder C:\inetpub instead. An upload folder the site really writes to may need Modify for that site's pool identity (IIS AppPool\<pool-name>); keep that grant on that folder only. More on icacls in Windows 11 shares.

    #Hunt for web shells

    Web shells are scripts dropped in the web root that run commands. List the 40 most recently changed script and config files:

    Get-ChildItem C:\inetpub -Recurse -File -Include *.aspx,*.asp,*.ashx,*.asmx,*.ascx,*.cshtml,*.php,*.jsp,*.cer,*.config -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 40 FullName,LastWriteTime,Length

    Search their contents for typical shell code:

    Get-ChildItem C:\inetpub -Recurse -File -Include *.aspx,*.asp,*.ashx,*.php,*.cshtml -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-String -Pattern 'cmd\.exe','powershell','Process\.Start','ProcessStartInfo','eval\(','Execute\(','shell_exec','passthru','base64_decode','WScript\.Shell' | Select-Object Path,LineNumber,Line

    Check wwwroot plus every physical path from Get-Website and every virtual directory from Get-WebVirtualDirectory. Delete confirmed shells after any related Forensics Question is answered, and check the IIS logs for the request that used them.

    Do not delete the site's real pages

    The default page (iisstart.htm, index.html, default.aspx) and app files the README mentions must stay. Remove only files that are clearly malicious or prohibited.

    PreviousRemove roles and featuresNextIIS FTP hardening
    SRV

    IIS FTP hardening

    jump:srv-ftp

    Fast path

    1. Read the README: does this server have to offer FTP?

    2. If not, stop the service and remove the feature from an elevated PowerShell window (details):

      Stop-Service ftpsvc
Set-Service ftpsvc -StartupType Disabled
Uninstall-WindowsFeature Web-Ftp-Server

    3. If FTP is required, turn off anonymous logons and turn on basic authentication on the FTP site:

      Import-Module WebAdministration
Set-ItemProperty 'IIS:\Sites\<ftp-site>' -Name ftpServer.security.authentication.anonymousAuthentication.enabled -Value $false
Set-ItemProperty 'IIS:\Sites\<ftp-site>' -Name ftpServer.security.authentication.basicAuthentication.enabled -Value $true

    4. Require SSL (how), isolate users (how) and tighten the authorization rules (how).

    5. Restart the service with Restart-Service ftpsvc.

    #Remove FTP when it is not required

    Stop-Service ftpsvc
Set-Service ftpsvc -StartupType Disabled
Uninstall-WindowsFeature Web-Ftp-Server

    Verify

    Get-WindowsFeature Web-Ftp-Server shows Available, and this returns nothing:

    Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 21 -State Listen -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    Also look for third-party FTP servers (FileZilla Server and others) in appwiz.cpl and in the services list, and remove them if they are not required.

    #Find the FTP site settings

    inetmgr > Sites > the FTP site. FTP sites show FTP icons: FTP Authentication, FTP Authorization Rules, FTP SSL Settings, FTP User Isolation, FTP Logging, FTP IP Address and Domain Restrictions. The server node holds defaults, and per-site settings override them, so always check the site itself.

    List FTP sites:

    Import-Module WebAdministration
Get-ChildItem IIS:\Sites | Where-Object { $_.bindings.Collection.protocol -contains 'ftp' } | Select-Object Name,State,PhysicalPath

    #Turn off anonymous FTP and turn on basic authentication

    inetmgr > FTP site > FTP Authentication > Anonymous Authentication > Disable, then Basic Authentication > Enable.

    Set-ItemProperty 'IIS:\Sites\<ftp-site>' -Name ftpServer.security.authentication.anonymousAuthentication.enabled -Value $false
Set-ItemProperty 'IIS:\Sites\<ftp-site>' -Name ftpServer.security.authentication.basicAuthentication.enabled -Value $true
Get-ItemProperty 'IIS:\Sites\<ftp-site>' -Name ftpServer.security.authentication.anonymousAuthentication.enabled

    %windir%\system32\inetsrv\appcmd set site /site.name:"<ftp-site>" /ftpServer.security.authentication.anonymousAuthentication.enabled:false

    Anonymous FTP required

    If the README says the server offers anonymous downloads, leave anonymous on and give anonymous users only Read in the authorization rules.

    #Require SSL (FTPS)

    GUI: inetmgr > FTP site > FTP SSL Settings > choose the SSL certificate > SSL Policy: Require SSL connections > Apply. Custom > Advanced sets the control and data channels separately.

    In PowerShell, pick a certificate from the machine store (or make one with New-SelfSignedCertificate, as in IIS HTTPS), then require SSL on both channels:

    $cert = Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\My | Select-Object -First 1
Set-ItemProperty 'IIS:\Sites\<ftp-site>' -Name ftpServer.security.ssl.serverCertHash -Value $cert.Thumbprint
Set-ItemProperty 'IIS:\Sites\<ftp-site>' -Name ftpServer.security.ssl.controlChannelPolicy -Value 'SslRequire'
Set-ItemProperty 'IIS:\Sites\<ftp-site>' -Name ftpServer.security.ssl.dataChannelPolicy -Value 'SslRequire'
    Attribute Allowed values Use
    controlChannelPolicy SslAllow, SslRequire, SslRequireCredentialsOnly SslRequire
    dataChannelPolicy SslAllow, SslRequire, SslDeny SslRequire

    A certificate must be selected before Require works.

    Requiring SSL breaks plain FTP clients

    If the README or the scoring check uses plain ftp.exe, which cannot do FTPS, requiring SSL makes the service look down. Apply it if the README asks for secure FTP or does not mention clients, and undo it if the score drops.

    #Turn on user isolation

    GUI: inetmgr > FTP site > FTP User Isolation > Isolate users. Restrict users to the following directory: User name directory (disable global virtual directories) > Apply.

    Set-ItemProperty 'IIS:\Sites\<ftp-site>' -Name ftpServer.userIsolation.mode -Value 'IsolateAllDirectories'
    Mode value IIS Manager option
    None Do not isolate users. Start users in: FTP root directory (the default)
    StartInUsersDirectory Do not isolate users. Start users in: User name directory
    IsolateAllDirectories Isolate users: User name directory (disable global virtual directories)
    IsolateRootDirectoryOnly Isolate users: User name physical directory (enable global virtual directories)
    ActiveDirectory Isolate users: FTP home directory configured in Active Directory
    Custom Isolate users: Custom (a custom provider)

    Each user's home folder must exist or that user cannot log in, so create the folders before turning isolation on:

    Account type Home folder under the FTP root
    Local user LocalUser\<username>
    Domain user <domain-netbios>\<username>
    Anonymous LocalUser\Public

    #Tighten authorization rules

    GUI: inetmgr > FTP site > FTP Authorization Rules. Remove Allow All Users Read, Write and any Allow Anonymous Users Write. Add Allow rules only for README users or groups, with only the permission they need. In rules, * means all users and ? means anonymous users.

    List the current rules:

    Get-WebConfiguration -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Location '<ftp-site>' -Filter 'system.ftpServer/security/authorization/add' | Select-Object accessType,users,roles,permissions

    Add a read-only rule for one group:

    Add-WebConfiguration -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Location '<ftp-site>' -Filter 'system.ftpServer/security/authorization' -Value @{accessType='Allow';roles='<groupname>';permissions='Read'}

    #Logging, logon attempt limits and IP restrictions

    • FTP Logging: enabled, W3C, directory %SystemDrive%\inetpub\logs\LogFiles.
    • FTP Logon Attempt Restrictions (server node): enable, for example 4 failed attempts in 30 seconds.
    • FTP IP Address and Domain Restrictions: allow only the subnet the README mentions (optional).
    • FTP Firewall Support (server node): the passive data port range. Keep matching firewall rules.
    • File system: the FTP root folder must not give Everyone or Users write unless uploads are required.

    Turn on logging for the site:

    Set-ItemProperty 'IIS:\Sites\<ftp-site>' -Name ftpServer.logFile.enabled -Value $true

    Turn on logon attempt restrictions server-wide (4 failures within 30 seconds blocks the client):

    Set-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Filter 'system.ftpServer/security/authentication/denyByFailure' -Name enabled -Value $true
Set-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Filter 'system.ftpServer/security/authentication/denyByFailure' -Name maxFailure -Value 4
Set-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Filter 'system.ftpServer/security/authentication/denyByFailure' -Name entryExpiration -Value '00:00:30'

    Restart the service after changes:

    Restart-Service ftpsvc
    PreviousIIS web server hardeningNextDNS and DHCP role hardening
    SRV

    DNS and DHCP role hardening

    jump:srv-dns-dhcp

    Fast path

    1. Open PowerShell as administrator and list the zones:

      Get-DnsServerZone | Format-Table ZoneName,ZoneType,IsDsIntegrated,DynamicUpdate,SecureSecondaries,IsAutoCreated -AutoSize

    2. For each zone that is not auto-created, stop zone transfers (skip if the README names a secondary DNS server):

      Set-DnsServerPrimaryZone -Name "<zone-name>" -SecureSecondaries NoTransfer

    3. For each AD-integrated zone, allow secure dynamic updates only:

      Set-DnsServerPrimaryZone -Name "<zone-name>" -DynamicUpdate Secure

    4. Check forwarders and look for wpad, wildcard and public-domain records (how).

    5. Turn on the global query block list with Set-DnsServerGlobalQueryBlockList -Enable $true.
    6. If DHCP is installed, confirm it is authorized and turn on audit logging (DHCP).

    #Open the DNS console and list zones

    Run dnsmgmt.msc (or Server Manager > Tools > DNS). Expand the server > Forward Lookup Zones and Reverse Lookup Zones. Server properties: right-click the server name > Properties.

    Get-DnsServerZone | Format-Table ZoneName,ZoneType,IsDsIntegrated,DynamicUpdate,SecureSecondaries,IsAutoCreated -AutoSize

    Ignore auto-created zones (0.in-addr.arpa, 127.in-addr.arpa, 255.in-addr.arpa) and TrustAnchors. On a DC you normally see the domain zone and _msdcs.<domain-name>.

    #Stop zone transfers

    GUI: dnsmgmt.msc > zone > Properties > Zone Transfers tab > clear Allow zone transfers, or choose Only to the following servers and list the README's secondary DNS server.

    No transfers at all:

    Set-DnsServerPrimaryZone -Name "<zone-name>" -SecureSecondaries NoTransfer

    Transfers only to listed servers:

    Set-DnsServerPrimaryZone -Name "<zone-name>" -SecureSecondaries TransferToSecureServers -SecondaryServers <ip-address>
    SecureSecondaries value Meaning
    NoTransfer No transfers (best)
    TransferToSecureServers Only to the IPs in -SecondaryServers
    TransferToZoneNameServer Only to servers in the zone's NS records
    TransferAnyServer Anyone can download the zone (bad)

    Check it with Get-DnsServerZone "<zone-name>" | Select-Object ZoneName,SecureSecondaries. Repeat for every zone that is not auto-created, reverse zones included.

    #Set dynamic updates to Secure only

    GUI: zone > Properties > General > Dynamic updates: Secure only. That option exists only on AD-integrated zones.

    Set-DnsServerPrimaryZone -Name "<zone-name>" -DynamicUpdate Secure
    DynamicUpdate value Meaning
    Secure Only authenticated domain members can register (best for AD zones)
    None No dynamic registration
    NonsecureAndSecure Anyone can register or overwrite records (bad)

    A file-backed (not AD-integrated) zone rejects Secure; use None there unless the README says clients register dynamically.

    Do not set DynamicUpdate None on the AD zones

    DCs register their SRV records through dynamic update. Setting the domain zone or _msdcs.<domain-name> to None stops that and slowly breaks AD. Use Secure.

    #Check recursion and forwarders

    Get-DnsServerRecursion
Get-DnsServerForwarder
    • On a DC that clients use for internet names, recursion must stay on, or clients cannot resolve outside sites. Disable it only if the README says the server is authoritative only: Set-DnsServerRecursion -Enable $false.
    • Forwarders should point to the README's resolvers, the ISP's, or a public resolver such as 8.8.8.8 or 1.1.1.1. An unknown IP is suspicious. Replace the list with Set-DnsServerForwarder -IPAddress <ip-address>.
    • Check conditional forwarders: Get-DnsServerZone | Where-Object ZoneType -eq 'Forwarder'.

    #Find malicious DNS records and zones

    All records in a zone, then A records only with their IPs:

    Get-DnsServerResourceRecord -ZoneName "<zone-name>" | Format-Table -AutoSize
Get-DnsServerResourceRecord -ZoneName "<zone-name>" -RRType A | Select-Object HostName,@{n='IP';e={$_.RecordData.IPv4Address}}

    Look for:

    • wpad or isatap records (proxy hijack). Remove unless the README needs them.
    • A wildcard * record.
    • Records for real outside sites, or whole zones named after public domains (a primary zone google.com or a bank's domain) that redirect users.
    • A records pointing the domain name or the DC's name to the wrong IP.

    #Remove a record or zone

    Remove one A record:

    Remove-DnsServerResourceRecord -ZoneName "<zone-name>" -RRType A -Name "<hostname>" -Force

    Remove a rogue zone:

    Remove-DnsServerZone -Name "<zone-name>" -Force

    #Turn on the global query block list

    The block list stops the server answering for wpad and isatap. It should be on:

    Get-DnsServerGlobalQueryBlockList
Set-DnsServerGlobalQueryBlockList -Enable $true

    #Other DNS server settings

    Setting Check Value
    Cache locking Get-DnsServerCache (LockingPercent) 100: Set-DnsServerCache -LockingPercent 100
    Secure cache against pollution Server Properties > Advanced, or Get-DnsServerCache (EnablePollutionProtection) On: Set-DnsServerCache -PollutionProtection $true
    Socket pool Get-DnsServerSetting -All (SocketPoolSize) 2500 by default; leave it or raise it
    Listen on Server Properties > Interfaces Only the server's real IPs (optional)
    Response rate limiting Get-DnsServerResponseRateLimiting Optional: Set-DnsServerResponseRateLimiting -Mode Enable
    DNSSEC zone > DNSSEC > Sign the Zone Only if the README asks
    Scavenging Server Properties > Advanced > Enable automatic scavenging of stale records Optional

    #Turn on DNS logging

    • dnsmgmt.msc > server > Properties > Event Logging > All events.
    • Debug Logging tab > Log packets for debugging, with a file path. Files grow fast, so use it only if the README wants query logging.
    • Analytic and audit logs: eventvwr.msc > View > Show Analytic and Debug Logs, then Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > DNS-Server. The Audit log is on by default; right-click Analytical > Enable Log for query logging.

    Check the diagnostic settings with Get-DnsServerDiagnostics.

    #Check DnsAdmins and the DNS plugin DLL

    Members of DnsAdmins can make the DNS service (SYSTEM on the DC) load any DLL, so keep the group empty (groups). Also look for a planted plugin. This should return nothing:

    Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters' -Name ServerLevelPluginDll -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    If it is set, remove it and restart DNS:

    Remove-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters' -Name ServerLevelPluginDll
Restart-Service DNS

    #DHCP: open the console

    Run dhcpmgmt.msc (or Server Manager > Tools > DHCP). Expand the server > IPv4 > Scope > Address Pool, Address Leases, Reservations and Scope Options. Server Options applies to every scope.

    #DHCP: check authorization in AD

    A domain-joined DHCP server must be authorized in AD or it will not hand out leases. List authorized servers, and authorize this one if it is missing:

    Get-DhcpServerInDC
Add-DhcpServerInDC -DnsName "<hostname>" -IPAddress <ip-address>

    <hostname> here is the server's full DNS name, for example dc1.corp.local. GUI: dhcpmgmt.msc > right-click DHCP > Manage authorized servers. An unknown server in the list is rogue:

    Remove-DhcpServerInDC -DnsName "<hostname>" -IPAddress <ip-address>

    #DHCP: turn on audit logging

    Get-DhcpServerAuditLog
Set-DhcpServerAuditLog -Enable $true

    GUI: dhcpmgmt.msc > right-click IPv4 > Properties > General > Enable DHCP audit logging. Logs go to %windir%\System32\dhcp.

    #DHCP: check scopes and options

    List scopes, server-wide options, options of one scope and its reservations:

    Get-DhcpServerv4Scope | Format-Table ScopeId,Name,StartRange,EndRange,SubnetMask,State,LeaseDuration -AutoSize
Get-DhcpServerv4OptionValue | Format-Table OptionId,Name,Value -AutoSize
Get-DhcpServerv4OptionValue -ScopeId <scope-id> | Format-Table OptionId,Name,Value -AutoSize
Get-DhcpServerv4Reservation -ScopeId <scope-id>
    Option Name Should be
    003 Router The real gateway from the README or network config
    006 DNS Servers The DC or README DNS servers, never an unknown IP
    015 DNS Domain Name The real domain
    252 WPAD Usually should not exist; remove it

    Set the DNS server and router for a scope. -Force skips the check that the DNS server answers:

    Set-DhcpServerv4OptionValue -ScopeId <scope-id> -DnsServer <dns-server-ip> -Router <default-gateway> -Force

    Remove a WPAD option:

    Remove-DhcpServerv4OptionValue -ScopeId <scope-id> -OptionId 252

    #DHCP: filters, groups and name protection

    • MAC allow and deny lists: Get-DhcpServerv4Filter and Get-DhcpServerv4FilterList.
    • The DHCP Administrators and DHCP Users groups should be empty or hold only README admins.
    • Turn on name protection: Set-DhcpServerv4DnsSetting -NameProtection $true.

    Restart after major changes with Restart-Service DHCPServer.

    PreviousIIS FTP hardeningNextFile server and SMB shares
    SRV

    File server and SMB shares

    jump:srv-smb

    Never remove SYSVOL or NETLOGON on a DC

    Removing them breaks Group Policy and domain logons for the whole domain. If they are missing, see troubleshooting.

    Fast path

    1. Open PowerShell as administrator and list the shares:

      Get-SmbShare | Format-Table Name,Path,Description -AutoSize

    2. Remove each share that is not default and not in the README (keep list):

      Remove-SmbShare -Name "<share-name>" -Force

    3. For each required share, replace Everyone with the README group:

      Revoke-SmbShareAccess -Name "<share-name>" -AccountName Everyone -Force
Grant-SmbShareAccess -Name "<share-name>" -AccountName "<domain-netbios>\<groupname>" -AccessRight Change -Force

    4. Harden the SMB server and remove SMB1:

      Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false -RequireSecuritySignature $true -EnableSecuritySignature $true -EncryptData $true -Force
Get-WindowsFeature FS-SMB1 | Where-Object Installed | Uninstall-WindowsFeature

    5. Check NTFS permissions on each shared folder with icacls "<path>" (how).

    #List shares and who can access them

    All shares, then the share permissions of every share whose name does not end in $:

    Get-SmbShare | Format-Table Name,Path,Description,EncryptData,FolderEnumerationMode -AutoSize
Get-SmbShare | Where-Object { $_.Name -notmatch '\$$' } | ForEach-Object { Get-SmbShareAccess -Name $_.Name } | Format-Table Name,AccountName,AccessControlType,AccessRight -AutoSize

    From cmd:

    net share

    GUI: fsmgmt.msc > Shared Folders > Shares (right-click a share > Properties > Share Permissions and Security tabs), or Server Manager > File and Storage Services > Shares.

    #Shares you must keep

    Share Keep? Notes
    ADMIN$ Keep Remote admin (C:\Windows)
    C$ and other drive $ shares Keep Default administrative shares
    IPC$ Keep Named pipes; required
    NETLOGON Keep on a DC Logon scripts; required for domain logons
    SYSVOL Keep on a DC GPOs; deleting it breaks Group Policy for the whole domain
    print$ Remove if not printing Created by Print Services
    Anything else Check the README Remove if not required; tighten if required

    #Remove an unauthorized share

    Remove-SmbShare -Name "<share-name>" -Force

    net share <share-name> /delete

    This only stops sharing; the folder and files stay. Check the folder for prohibited media, hacking tools and password lists (prohibited files).

    #Tighten share permissions on a required share

    The usual planted entry is Everyone Full. Remove it, grant the README group, and read the result:

    Revoke-SmbShareAccess -Name "<share-name>" -AccountName Everyone -Force
Grant-SmbShareAccess -Name "<share-name>" -AccountName "<domain-netbios>\<groupname>" -AccessRight Change -Force
Get-SmbShareAccess -Name "<share-name>"

    AccessRight values are Read, Change and Full. Deny entries you did not expect come from Block-SmbShareAccess; remove them with Unblock-SmbShareAccess. Effective access is the more restrictive of the share permission and the NTFS permission.

    #Turn on access-based enumeration

    Users then see only the folders they can open:

    Set-SmbShare -Name "<share-name>" -FolderEnumerationMode AccessBased -Force

    #Fix NTFS permissions with icacls

    Show the ACL, remove Everyone's explicit grants recursively, and grant the README group Modify:

    icacls "<path>"
icacls "<path>" /remove:g Everyone /T
icacls "<path>" /grant "<domain-netbios>\<groupname>:(OI)(CI)M"
    • (OI)(CI) applies the entry to files and subfolders. F is full, M modify, RX read and execute, R read, W write.
    • /remove:g removes explicit allow entries only. Inherited entries, marked (I), must be fixed on the parent folder or by breaking inheritance.
    • /inheritance:d converts inherited entries to explicit ones; /inheritance:r removes them. After either, confirm Administrators and SYSTEM still have F.
    • icacls "<path>" /reset /T makes a folder inherit from its parent again.

    GUI: folder > Properties > Security > Advanced. Taking ownership and the rest of icacls work as on Windows 11.

    #Harden the SMB server configuration

    Apply the settings and read them back:

    Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false -RequireSecuritySignature $true -EnableSecuritySignature $true -EncryptData $true -RejectUnencryptedAccess $true -Force
Get-SmbServerConfiguration | Select-Object EnableSMB1Protocol,EnableSMB2Protocol,RequireSecuritySignature,EnableSecuritySignature,EncryptData,RejectUnencryptedAccess
    Setting Value Notes
    EnableSMB1Protocol False Also remove the FS-SMB1 feature
    EnableSMB2Protocol True Never set it False; that turns off SMB 2 and 3 entirely
    RequireSecuritySignature True Same as the GPO setting Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always)
    EncryptData True Clients without SMB 3 cannot connect while RejectUnencryptedAccess is True
    RejectUnencryptedAccess True (default) Only matters when EncryptData is True
    AutoShareServer True (default) False removes ADMIN$ and C$; leave the default
    AuditSmb1Access Optional -AuditSmb1Access $true logs SMB1 attempts

    Outgoing SMB from this server:

    Set-SmbClientConfiguration -RequireSecuritySignature $true -Force

    #Signing on a DC comes from the GPO

    The Default Domain Controllers Policy sets Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always) to Enabled by default. If someone changed it to Disabled, the GPO reverts your PowerShell change at the next refresh, so fix the GPO (GPO).

    #Encryption and older clients

    Server-wide encryption with RejectUnencryptedAccess blocks clients without SMB 3 encryption (Windows 7, old Samba, many printers and scanners). The scoring engine checks the setting locally, so it is normally safe. If a README-required client stops connecting, turn server-wide encryption off and encrypt only the share:

    Set-SmbShare -Name "<share-name>" -EncryptData $true -Force

    #Check open files and sessions

    Get-SmbSession | Format-Table SessionId,ClientComputerName,ClientUserName,NumOpens -AutoSize
Get-SmbOpenFile | Format-Table ClientUserName,Path -AutoSize

    Close a suspicious session by its SessionId:

    Close-SmbSession -SessionId <session-id> -Force

    #File Server Resource Manager file screens

    If the FS-Resource-Manager role service is installed (fsrm.msc), it can block file types (file screens) and set quotas. The README may ask for a file screen, for example blocking audio and video in a share:

    New-FsrmFileScreen -Path "<path>" -Template "Block Audio and Video Files"
Get-FsrmFileScreen

    Skip this unless the README mentions it. Do not install FSRM just for points.

    PreviousDNS and DHCP role hardeningNextRDP and WinRM on Server
    SRV

    RDP and WinRM on Server

    jump:srv-rdp

    Check the README before turning off RDP

    Servers are often administered remotely. If the README says RDP or remote management is required, keep it on and harden it. If it says nothing, turning RDP off is normally the secure choice. Do not turn off WinRM on a DC; Server Manager uses it.

    Fast path

    1. Read the README: is Remote Desktop required?

    2. If not, turn it off and disable its firewall rules from an elevated PowerShell window:

      Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server' -Name fDenyTSConnections -Value 1
Disable-NetFirewallRule -DisplayGroup "Remote Desktop"

    3. If it is required, require NLA, TLS and high encryption (details):

      Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp' -Name UserAuthentication -Value 1
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp' -Name SecurityLayer -Value 2
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp' -Name MinEncryptionLevel -Value 3

    4. Check that Remote Desktop Users holds only README users (how).

    5. Turn off WinRM Basic auth and unencrypted traffic:

      Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Service\AllowUnencrypted -Value $false
Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Service\Auth\Basic -Value $false

    #Turn off Remote Desktop when not required

    GUI: Server Manager > Local Server > Remote Desktop > Don't allow remote connections to this computer, or sconfig option 7.

    Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server' -Name fDenyTSConnections -Value 1
Disable-NetFirewallRule -DisplayGroup "Remote Desktop"

    Verify

    This should print 1:

    (Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server').fDenyTSConnections

    On a DC a GPO can override the registry value: Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Remote Desktop Services > Remote Desktop Session Host > Connections > Allow users to connect remotely by using Remote Desktop Services. If that policy is set, it writes fDenyTSConnections under HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services, which wins.

    #Harden Remote Desktop when it is required

    Allow connections, require Network Level Authentication, require the TLS security layer (2) and High encryption (3), and allow the firewall rules:

    Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server' -Name fDenyTSConnections -Value 0
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp' -Name UserAuthentication -Value 1
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp' -Name SecurityLayer -Value 2
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp' -Name MinEncryptionLevel -Value 3
Enable-NetFirewallRule -DisplayGroup "Remote Desktop"

    GUI for NLA: sysdm.cpl > Remote tab > Allow remote connections to this computer, and check Allow connections only from computers running Remote Desktop with Network Level Authentication.

    #RDP settings by GPO on a DC

    On a DC use the GPO: Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Remote Desktop Services > Remote Desktop Session Host > Security. On a standalone server the same path is in gpedit.msc under Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates.

    Policy Value
    Require user authentication for remote connections by using Network Level Authentication Enabled
    Require use of specific security layer for remote (RDP) connections Enabled, SSL
    Set client connection encryption level Enabled, High Level
    Always prompt for password upon connection Enabled
    Do not allow passwords to be saved (under Remote Desktop Connection Client) Enabled

    #Limit which users can connect by RDP

    • Builtin Remote Desktop Users should hold only README-listed RDP users. Administrators can RDP without being in it.
    • On a DC, the Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services right in the Default Domain Controllers Policy controls access (Administrators by default). Ordinary domain users cannot RDP to a DC unless added there.
    • Add Guests to Deny log on through Remote Desktop Services.

    On a DC:

    Get-ADGroupMember "Remote Desktop Users" | Select-Object SamAccountName

    On a standalone server:

    Get-LocalGroupMember "Remote Desktop Users"

    #Set session time limits

    Path: same Remote Desktop Session Host folder > Session Time Limits.

    Policy Value
    Set time limit for active but idle Remote Desktop Services sessions Enabled, 15 minutes
    Set time limit for disconnected sessions Enabled, 1 minute (or 15)
    End session when time limits are reached Enabled

    Also under Device and Resource Redirection: Do not allow drive redirection = Enabled, and optionally Do not allow Clipboard redirection = Enabled.

    #Harden WinRM and PowerShell remoting

    Show the service config, turn off unencrypted traffic and Basic auth on both service and client, and list who may connect:

    winrm get winrm/config/service
Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Service\AllowUnencrypted -Value $false
Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Service\Auth\Basic -Value $false
Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Client\AllowUnencrypted -Value $false
Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Client\Auth\Basic -Value $false
Get-PSSessionConfiguration | Select-Object Name,Permission

    Server 2022 has WinRM on by default (HTTP port 5985, Kerberos authentication, message-level encryption). Keep it running unless the README says otherwise.

    GPO equivalent: Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Windows Remote Management (WinRM) > WinRM Service. Set Allow Basic authentication to Disabled, Allow unencrypted traffic to Disabled, and Disallow WinRM from storing RunAs credentials to Enabled.

    Remote Management Users should be empty unless the README requires it.

    #Check TrustedHosts

    TrustedHosts set to * allows this server to send credentials to any host. Read it, and clear it:

    Get-Item WSMan:\localhost\Client\TrustedHosts
Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Client\TrustedHosts -Value '' -Force

    #Turn WinRM off completely

    Only if the README allows it, you are not managing remotely, and the server is not a DC:

    Disable-PSRemoting -Force
Stop-Service WinRM
Set-Service WinRM -StartupType Disabled
    WinRM over HTTPS

    An HTTPS listener on 5986 needs a certificate that matches the server name. Create one with winrm quickconfig -transport:https. Do it only if the README asks; it is rarely scored.

    PreviousFile server and SMB sharesNextServer services (disable or keep)
    SRV

    Server services (disable or keep)

    jump:srv-services

    Hunting non-Microsoft services, malicious binary paths and service permissions works as on Windows 11 services and malware hunting. The tables below cover what is different on Server.

    Fast path

    1. Open PowerShell as administrator.

    2. On a DC, confirm the core AD services are running and Automatic:

      Get-Service NTDS,DNS,Netlogon,Kdc,W32Time,DFSR,ADWS,IsmServ | Format-Table Name,Status,StartType -AutoSize

    3. Disable a service the README does not need (list):

      Stop-Service -Name <service-name> -Force
Set-Service -Name <service-name> -StartupType Disabled

    4. On a DC, disable Print Spooler unless the README requires printing.

    5. Confirm every README-required service is still Running with Get-Service <service-name>.

    #Disable a service

    Stop-Service -Name <service-name> -Force
Set-Service -Name <service-name> -StartupType Disabled
Get-Service -Name <service-name> | Select-Object Name,Status,StartType

    sc.exe config <service-name> start= disabled
sc.exe stop <service-name>

    services.msc > double-click the service > Startup type: Disabled > Stop > OK.

    To undo, set the startup type back to Automatic (or Manual) and start the service:

    Set-Service -Name <service-name> -StartupType Automatic
Start-Service -Name <service-name>

    #Services to disable unless the README requires them

    Service name Display name Notes
    Spooler Print Spooler Disable on a DC (PrintNightmare, coercion attacks). Keep if the README requires printing
    RemoteRegistry Remote Registry Disable
    SNMP SNMP Service Remove the SNMP-Service feature
    SNMPTRAP SNMP Trap Disable
    simptcp Simple TCP/IP Services Remove the Simple-TCPIP feature
    ftpsvc Microsoft FTP Service Only if FTP is not required
    W3SVC and WAS World Wide Web Publishing Service, Windows Process Activation Service Only if IIS is not required (other features can use WAS)
    WMSVC Web Management Service IIS remote management; disable if not needed
    SMTPSVC Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) Disable unless the README needs mail
    RemoteAccess Routing and Remote Access Disable unless VPN or routing is required
    SharedAccess Internet Connection Sharing (ICS) Disable
    SSDPSRV and upnphost SSDP Discovery, UPnP Device Host Disable
    WebClient WebClient (WebDAV client) Disable if present
    Fax Fax Disable or remove the feature
    XblAuthManager, XblGameSave Xbox Live services Present on Desktop Experience; disable
    sshd OpenSSH SSH Server Only if the README does not require SSH
    TermService Remote Desktop Services Only if RDP is not required
    TlntSvr, third-party FTP or VNC servers Various Not part of Server 2022; uninstall the software

    #Services that must stay on a domain controller

    Service name Display name Why
    NTDS Active Directory Domain Services The AD database itself
    Kdc Kerberos Key Distribution Center Every Kerberos logon
    Netlogon Netlogon DC locator, secure channel, NETLOGON and SYSVOL shares
    DNS DNS Server AD depends on DNS SRV records
    W32Time Windows Time Kerberos fails if clocks differ by more than 5 minutes
    DFSR DFS Replication Replicates SYSVOL
    Dfs DFS Namespace Serves \\<domain-name>\SYSVOL and \\<domain-name>\NETLOGON
    ADWS Active Directory Web Services The AD PowerShell module and ADAC need it
    IsmServ Intersite Messaging AD replication between sites
    LanmanServer Server SMB file sharing (SYSVOL, NETLOGON)
    LanmanWorkstation Workstation SMB client
    RpcSs and RpcEptMapper Remote Procedure Call (RPC), RPC Endpoint Mapper Everything
    SamSs Security Accounts Manager Authentication
    Dnscache DNS Client Name resolution
    EventLog Windows Event Log Auditing
    gpsvc Group Policy Client Applies GPOs
    mpssvc Windows Defender Firewall Keep running
    WinDefend Microsoft Defender Antivirus Service Keep running
    WinRM Windows Remote Management (WS-Management) Server Manager, remote admin
    CertSvc Active Directory Certificate Services Only if AD CS is installed

    #Services each role needs

    Role Services
    DNS DNS
    DHCP DHCPServer
    IIS W3SVC, WAS, AppHostSvc (Application Host Helper Service)
    IIS FTP ftpsvc
    File server LanmanServer (plus SrmSvc for FSRM, DFSR and Dfs for DFS)
    RDP TermService, SessionEnv, UmRdpService
    Print server Spooler
    SSH sshd

    #How not to break AD

    • Never set NTDS, Netlogon, Kdc, DNS, DFSR, W32Time or LanmanServer to Disabled on a DC.
    • Do not delete the Active Directory Domain Services or DNS Service firewall rule groups.
    • Do not change the DC's IP address or its DNS client settings. A DC points to itself (127.0.0.1 or its own IP).
    • Do not remove Authenticated Users from Access this computer from the network in the DC policy.
    • After a big change, run dcdiag /q and gpupdate /force. New errors mean undo.

    #A service keeps coming back

    On a DC, a GPO can force a service's startup type (Computer Configuration > Policies > Windows Settings > Security Settings > System Services). If a service you disabled keeps returning, or one you need keeps getting disabled, look there in every GPO (GPO report).

    PreviousRDP and WinRM on ServerNextUpdates and Defender on Server
    SRV

    Updates and Defender on Server

    jump:srv-updates-defender

    Fast path

    1. Open PowerShell as administrator and run sconfig.
    2. Choose 5 (Update setting), then A (Automatic).
    3. Choose 6 (Install updates), then 1 (all quality updates), then A to install all of them. Keep working while it runs.

    4. Check Defender in a second PowerShell window:

      Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object AMServiceEnabled,AntivirusEnabled,RealTimeProtectionEnabled,AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated

    5. If that errors because Defender is missing, reinstall it and restart (details):

      Install-WindowsFeature -Name Windows-Defender

    6. Remove planted exclusions listed by Get-MpPreference (how).

    7. Turn IE Enhanced Security Configuration on for Administrators and Users in Server Manager > Local Server.

    #Install updates with sconfig

    1. Run sconfig in an elevated PowerShell window.
    2. Option 5 (Update setting) > A (Automatic) to install updates on a schedule.
    3. Option 6 (Install updates) > 1 (all quality updates) or 2 (recommended quality updates only).
    4. When the list appears, type A to install all of them.

    Start updates early

    Updates are slow. Start them in the first 30 minutes and keep working. Do not reboot in the middle of a GPO or AD change.

    #Install updates from Settings

    Start > Settings > Update & Security > Windows Update > Check for updates. Server 2022 uses the Windows 10 style Settings app. Advanced options can include updates for other Microsoft products.

    #Keep the update services running

    Check the services, and set Windows Update back to Manual (its default trigger start) and start it if it was disabled:

    Get-Service wuauserv,UsoSvc,BITS | Select-Object Name,Status,StartType
Set-Service wuauserv -StartupType Manual
Start-Service wuauserv

    The full list of update services and their defaults is in Windows 11 updates.

    #Remove policies that block updates

    Read the Windows Update policy keys:

    Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    NoAutoUpdate = 1, or a WUServer pointing at an unknown host, is planted. On a standalone server delete the value as on Windows 11. On a DC fix the GPO that sets it (Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Windows Update): set Configure Automatic Updates to Enabled with option 4 (Auto download and schedule the install), and remove any intranet update service location you do not recognize.

    #Check Defender status on Server

    Get-WindowsFeature Windows-Defender
Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object AMServiceEnabled,AntivirusEnabled,RealTimeProtectionEnabled,BehaviorMonitorEnabled,IoavProtectionEnabled,AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated,IsTamperProtected

    Every Enabled value should be True and the signatures recent. GUI: Server Manager > Local Server > Microsoft Defender Antivirus, or Start > Windows Security (present on Server 2022 with Desktop Experience).

    #Reinstall Defender if it was removed

    Install-WindowsFeature -Name Windows-Defender
Restart-Computer

    After the reboot, update signatures and check status:

    Update-MpSignature
Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object AMServiceEnabled,AntivirusEnabled,RealTimeProtectionEnabled

    If Get-WindowsFeature Windows-Defender shows Removed, the payload was deleted and you need install media, for example Install-WindowsFeature Windows-Defender -Source wim:D:\sources\install.wim:<index> with the index of your edition. That is rarely possible in competition.

    #Turn Defender protections back on

    Turn the protections back on, then list exclusions and remove any that were planted:

    Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $false -DisableBehaviorMonitoring $false -DisableIOAVProtection $false -DisableScriptScanning $false -MAPSReporting Advanced -SubmitSamplesConsent SendSafeSamples -PUAProtection Enabled
Get-MpPreference | Select-Object ExclusionPath,ExclusionExtension,ExclusionProcess,ExclusionIpAddress

    Remove one exclusion (use -ExclusionExtension or -ExclusionProcess for the other kinds):

    Remove-MpPreference -ExclusionPath "<path>"

    #Remove policies that disable Defender

    Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Real-Time Protection' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    DisableAntiSpyware = 1 or DisableRealtimeMonitoring = 1 there is planted. Delete the value on a standalone server (Windows 11 steps). On a DC fix the GPO under Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus.

    #Leave the automatic role exclusions alone

    Defender on Server automatically excludes AD DS, DNS, DHCP, IIS and SYSVOL paths. They do not appear in Get-MpPreference and you cannot and should not remove them. DisableAutoExclusions should stay False. Remove only exclusions that Get-MpPreference lists.

    Scans, ASR rules and threat history work as on Windows 11.

    #Turn IE Enhanced Security Configuration back on

    GUI: Server Manager > Local Server > IE Enhanced Security Configuration > On for both Administrators and Users. This is the preferred method because it also updates running sessions.

    PowerShell sets IsInstalled = 1 on the Administrators key (A7) and the Users key (A8), then reads them back:

    $admin = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Active Setup\Installed Components\{A509B1A7-37EF-4b3f-8CFC-4F3A74704073}'
$user = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Active Setup\Installed Components\{A509B1A8-37EF-4b3f-8CFC-4F3A74704073}'
Set-ItemProperty $admin -Name IsInstalled -Value 1
Set-ItemProperty $user -Name IsInstalled -Value 1
Get-ItemProperty $admin,$user | Select-Object PSChildName,IsInstalled

    After the registry method, log off and back on for it to take full effect.

    PreviousServer services (disable or keep)NextServer recon and fix scripts
    SRV

    Server recon and fix scripts

    jump:srv-scripts

    Fast path

    1. Open PowerShell as administrator (Start, type powershell, Run as administrator).

    2. Allow scripts in this window only:

      Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Force

    3. Paste the whole recon script and press Enter. It changes nothing.

    4. Read server_recon.txt, which opens in Notepad. Press Ctrl+F and search ===== to jump between parts.
    5. Run only the fix snippets that match the README.

    #Read-only recon script

    The script works on a standalone server, a member server or a DC, and changes nothing. It writes server_recon.txt to your desktop and opens it in Notepad. Paste it into an elevated PowerShell window, or save it as recon.ps1 and run powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\recon.ps1.

    What it does, in order:

    1. Creates the report file and three small helpers: Sec writes a ===== header, W formats output as a table, and T runs one check and writes its result (or the error) under a header, so one failing check never stops the rest.
    2. Reads the domain role and decides whether this is a DC.
    3. On a DC with the AD module: domain and forest, every user with description and logon script, members of each privileged group, direct members of Builtin Administrators, the raw Pre-Windows 2000 Compatible Access members, users whose primary group is not Domain Users, users with risky flags, users with SPNs, locked-out users, users and non-DC computers trusted for delegation, the domain and fine-grained password policies, MachineAccountQuota, Recycle Bin state, every GPO and link, SYSVOL cpassword hits, LDAP signing and Netlogon registry values, and dcdiag /q.
    4. On a DC without the AD module: writes the command that installs it.
    5. On a standalone or member server: local users, local Administrators and Remote Desktop Users members, and net accounts.
    6. On every server: installed features, SMB configuration, shares and share permissions, listening TCP and UDP ports with process names, non-Microsoft services, running services, scheduled tasks outside \Microsoft\, Defender status, exclusions and policy keys, firewall profiles, RDP and NLA values, WinRM settings, LSA values, Windows Update policy, Print Spooler state and IE ESC state.
    7. When the roles exist: DNS zones, forwarders, recursion and plugin DLL; DHCP authorization, audit log and scopes; IIS sites, app pools, server-wide directory browsing and FTP site settings.
    8. Writes Done and opens the report.
    $out = Join-Path ([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Desktop')) 'server_recon.txt'
"Server recon $(Get-Date) on $env:COMPUTERNAME as $env:USERDOMAIN\$env:USERNAME" | Out-File $out -Encoding utf8
function Sec([string]$t) { "`r`n===== $t =====" | Out-File $out -Append -Encoding utf8 }
function W { $input | Format-Table -AutoSize -Wrap | Out-String -Width 4096 | Out-File $out -Append -Encoding utf8 }
function T([string]$name, [scriptblock]$sb) { Sec $name; try { & $sb 2>&1 | W } catch { "ERROR: $($_.Exception.Message)" | Out-File $out -Append -Encoding utf8 } }

$cs = Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem
$isDC = $cs.DomainRole -ge 4
T 'Operating system' { Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object Caption,Version,BuildNumber,LastBootUpTime }
T 'Domain role' { [pscustomobject]@{DomainRole=$cs.DomainRole; IsDC=$isDC; PartOfDomain=$cs.PartOfDomain; Domain=$cs.Domain} }

if ($isDC -and (Get-Module -ListAvailable ActiveDirectory)) {
  Import-Module ActiveDirectory
  T 'Domain' { Get-ADDomain | Select-Object DNSRoot,NetBIOSName,DomainMode,PDCEmulator }
  T 'Forest' { Get-ADForest | Select-Object Name,ForestMode,SchemaMaster }
  T 'All domain users' { Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties LastLogonDate,Description,ScriptPath | Sort-Object SamAccountName | Select-Object SamAccountName,Enabled,LastLogonDate,Description,ScriptPath }
  $groups = 'Domain Admins','Enterprise Admins','Schema Admins','Administrators','Account Operators','Backup Operators','Server Operators','Print Operators','DnsAdmins','Group Policy Creator Owners','Remote Desktop Users','Remote Management Users','Protected Users'
  foreach ($g in $groups) { T "Group: $g" { Get-ADGroupMember -Identity $g -Recursive -ErrorAction Stop | Select-Object SamAccountName,objectClass } }
  T 'Builtin Administrators direct members' { Get-ADGroupMember -Identity Administrators | Select-Object SamAccountName,objectClass }
  T 'Pre-Windows 2000 Compatible Access raw members' { (Get-ADGroup 'Pre-Windows 2000 Compatible Access' -Properties member).member }
  T 'Primary group not Domain Users' { Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties PrimaryGroupID | Where-Object { $_.PrimaryGroupID -ne 513 } | Select-Object SamAccountName,PrimaryGroupID }
  T 'Risky user flags' {
    Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties PasswordNeverExpires,PasswordNotRequired,DoesNotRequirePreAuth,AllowReversiblePasswordEncryption,CannotChangePassword,UseDESKeyOnly,TrustedForDelegation,AccountNotDelegated,AdminCount |
      Where-Object { $_.PasswordNeverExpires -or $_.PasswordNotRequired -or $_.DoesNotRequirePreAuth -or $_.AllowReversiblePasswordEncryption -or $_.CannotChangePassword -or $_.UseDESKeyOnly -or $_.TrustedForDelegation -or $_.AdminCount -eq 1 } |
      Select-Object SamAccountName,Enabled,PasswordNeverExpires,PasswordNotRequired,DoesNotRequirePreAuth,AllowReversiblePasswordEncryption,CannotChangePassword,UseDESKeyOnly,TrustedForDelegation,AccountNotDelegated,AdminCount
  }
  T 'Users with SPNs' { Get-ADUser -Filter 'ServicePrincipalName -like "*"' -Properties ServicePrincipalName | Select-Object SamAccountName,@{n='SPN';e={$_.ServicePrincipalName -join '; '}} }
  T 'Locked out users' { Search-ADAccount -LockedOut -UsersOnly | Select-Object SamAccountName }
  T 'Computers trusted for delegation (DCs are normal)' { Get-ADComputer -Filter 'TrustedForDelegation -eq $true' | Select-Object Name }
  T 'Default domain password policy' { Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy | Select-Object MinPasswordLength,ComplexityEnabled,PasswordHistoryCount,MaxPasswordAge,MinPasswordAge,LockoutThreshold,LockoutDuration,LockoutObservationWindow,ReversibleEncryptionEnabled }
  T 'Fine-grained password policies' { Get-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicy -Filter * | Select-Object Name,Precedence,MinPasswordLength,ComplexityEnabled,LockoutThreshold,ReversibleEncryptionEnabled,@{n='AppliesTo';e={$_.AppliesTo -join '; '}} }
  T 'MachineAccountQuota' { Get-ADObject (Get-ADDomain).DistinguishedName -Properties 'ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota' | Select-Object 'ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota' }
  T 'Recycle Bin' { Get-ADOptionalFeature -Filter 'Name -like "Recycle Bin Feature"' | Select-Object Name,@{n='Enabled';e={[bool]$_.EnabledScopes}} }
  if (Get-Module -ListAvailable GroupPolicy) {
    Import-Module GroupPolicy
    T 'GPOs' { Get-GPO -All | Sort-Object ModificationTime -Descending | Select-Object DisplayName,GpoStatus,ModificationTime,Id }
    T 'GPO links' {
      $targets = @((Get-ADDomain).DistinguishedName) + @(Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter * | Select-Object -ExpandProperty DistinguishedName)
      foreach ($x in $targets) { (Get-GPInheritance -Target $x).GpoLinks | Select-Object Order,DisplayName,Enabled,Enforced,Target }
    }
  }
  T 'SYSVOL cpassword hits' { Get-ChildItem C:\Windows\SYSVOL\sysvol -Recurse -Include *.xml -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-String 'cpassword' | Select-Object Path }
  T 'LDAP signing and channel binding' { Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NTDS\Parameters' | Select-Object LDAPServerIntegrity,LdapEnforceChannelBinding }
  T 'Netlogon parameters' { Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Netlogon\Parameters' | Select-Object SysvolReady,RequireSignOrSeal,RequireStrongKey,FullSecureChannelProtection }
  T 'dcdiag /q' { dcdiag /q }
} elseif ($isDC) {
  Sec 'AD module missing'
  'Run: Install-WindowsFeature RSAT-AD-PowerShell' | Out-File $out -Append -Encoding utf8
} else {
  T 'Local users' { Get-LocalUser | Select-Object Name,Enabled,PasswordRequired,PasswordExpires,LastLogon,Description }
  T 'Local Administrators' { Get-LocalGroupMember Administrators | Select-Object Name,ObjectClass,PrincipalSource }
  T 'Local Remote Desktop Users' { Get-LocalGroupMember 'Remote Desktop Users' | Select-Object Name,ObjectClass }
  T 'net accounts (local policy)' { net accounts }
}

T 'Installed roles and features' { Get-WindowsFeature | Where-Object Installed | Select-Object Name,DisplayName }
T 'SMB server config' { Get-SmbServerConfiguration | Select-Object EnableSMB1Protocol,EnableSMB2Protocol,RequireSecuritySignature,EncryptData,RejectUnencryptedAccess }
T 'Shares' { Get-SmbShare | Select-Object Name,Path,Description }
T 'Share permissions (non-$ shares)' { Get-SmbShare | Where-Object { $_.Name -notmatch '\$$' } | ForEach-Object { Get-SmbShareAccess -Name $_.Name } | Select-Object Name,AccountName,AccessControlType,AccessRight }
T 'Listening TCP ports' { Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen | Sort-Object LocalPort | Select-Object LocalAddress,LocalPort,OwningProcess,@{n='Process';e={(Get-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).ProcessName}} }
T 'Listening UDP ports' { Get-NetUDPEndpoint | Sort-Object LocalPort | Select-Object LocalAddress,LocalPort,OwningProcess,@{n='Process';e={(Get-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).ProcessName}} -Unique }
T 'Non-Microsoft services' {
  Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | ForEach-Object {
    $exe = if ($_.PathName -match '^\s*"?([^"]+?\.exe)') { $Matches[1] } else { $_.PathName }
    $co = try { (Get-Item $exe -ErrorAction Stop).VersionInfo.CompanyName } catch { '?' }
    if ($co -notlike '*Microsoft*') { [pscustomobject]@{Name=$_.Name; State=$_.State; Start=$_.StartMode; Company=$co; Path=$_.PathName} }
  }
}
T 'Running services' { Get-Service | Where-Object Status -eq 'Running' | Sort-Object Name | Select-Object Name,DisplayName,StartType }
T 'Scheduled tasks outside \Microsoft\' { Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object { $_.TaskPath -notlike '\Microsoft\*' } | Select-Object TaskPath,TaskName,State,@{n='Action';e={($_.Actions | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Execute) $($_.Arguments)" }) -join '; '}} }
T 'Defender status' { Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object AMServiceEnabled,AntivirusEnabled,RealTimeProtectionEnabled,BehaviorMonitorEnabled,AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated }
T 'Defender exclusions' { Get-MpPreference | Select-Object ExclusionPath,ExclusionExtension,ExclusionProcess,ExclusionIpAddress }
T 'Defender policy keys' { Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender','HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Real-Time Protection' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object PSChildName,DisableAntiSpyware,DisableRealtimeMonitoring }
T 'Firewall profiles' { Get-NetFirewallProfile | Select-Object Name,Enabled,DefaultInboundAction,DefaultOutboundAction,LogBlocked }
T 'RDP enabled (fDenyTSConnections 0 means on)' { Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server' | Select-Object fDenyTSConnections }
T 'RDP security (UserAuthentication 1 means NLA)' { Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp' | Select-Object UserAuthentication,SecurityLayer,MinEncryptionLevel }
T 'WinRM service settings' { Get-ChildItem WSMan:\localhost\Service | Select-Object Name,Value }
T 'WinRM service auth' { Get-ChildItem WSMan:\localhost\Service\Auth | Select-Object Name,Value }
T 'WinRM TrustedHosts' { Get-Item WSMan:\localhost\Client\TrustedHosts | Select-Object Name,Value }
T 'LSA settings' { Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa' | Select-Object LmCompatibilityLevel,NoLMHash,RestrictAnonymous,RestrictAnonymousSAM,EveryoneIncludesAnonymous,DsrmAdminLogonBehavior }
T 'Windows Update policy' { Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate','HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object PSChildName,WUServer,NoAutoUpdate,AUOptions }
T 'Update and spooler services' { Get-Service wuauserv,UsoSvc,BITS,Spooler -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name,Status,StartType }
T 'IE ESC (A7 admins, A8 users, IsInstalled 1 means on)' { Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Active Setup\Installed Components\{A509B1A7-37EF-4b3f-8CFC-4F3A74704073}','HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Active Setup\Installed Components\{A509B1A8-37EF-4b3f-8CFC-4F3A74704073}' | Select-Object PSChildName,IsInstalled }

if ((Get-Service DNS -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -and (Get-Module -ListAvailable DnsServer)) {
  T 'DNS zones' { Get-DnsServerZone | Select-Object ZoneName,ZoneType,IsDsIntegrated,IsAutoCreated,DynamicUpdate,SecureSecondaries }
  T 'DNS forwarders' { Get-DnsServerForwarder | Select-Object @{n='IPAddress';e={$_.IPAddress -join ', '}},UseRootHint }
  T 'DNS recursion' { Get-DnsServerRecursion | Select-Object Enable,SecureResponse }
  T 'DNS plugin DLL (should be empty)' { Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\DNS\Parameters' | Select-Object ServerLevelPluginDll }
}
if ((Get-Service DHCPServer -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -and (Get-Module -ListAvailable DhcpServer)) {
  T 'DHCP authorized servers' { Get-DhcpServerInDC }
  T 'DHCP audit log' { Get-DhcpServerAuditLog | Select-Object Enable,Path }
  T 'DHCP scopes' { Get-DhcpServerv4Scope | Select-Object ScopeId,Name,StartRange,EndRange,State }
}
if ((Get-Service W3SVC,ftpsvc -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) -and (Get-Module -ListAvailable WebAdministration)) {
  Import-Module WebAdministration
  T 'IIS sites' { Get-Website | Select-Object Name,State,PhysicalPath,@{n='Bindings';e={($_.bindings.Collection | ForEach-Object { "$($_.protocol) $($_.bindingInformation)" }) -join '; '}} }
  T 'IIS app pools' { Get-ChildItem IIS:\AppPools | Select-Object Name,State,@{n='Identity';e={$_.processModel.identityType}},@{n='User';e={$_.processModel.userName}} }
  T 'IIS directory browsing (server default)' { [pscustomobject]@{Enabled=(Get-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Filter 'system.webServer/directoryBrowse' -Name enabled).Value} }
  T 'FTP sites' { Get-ChildItem IIS:\Sites | Where-Object { $_.bindings.Collection.protocol -contains 'ftp' } | Select-Object Name,State,@{n='Anonymous';e={$_.ftpServer.security.authentication.anonymousAuthentication.enabled}},@{n='Basic';e={$_.ftpServer.security.authentication.basicAuthentication.enabled}},@{n='ControlSSL';e={$_.ftpServer.security.ssl.controlChannelPolicy}},@{n='DataSSL';e={$_.ftpServer.security.ssl.dataChannelPolicy}},@{n='Isolation';e={$_.ftpServer.userIsolation.mode}} }
}
"`r`nDone." | Out-File $out -Append -Encoding utf8
notepad $out

    What deserves a second look

    Compare everything under Group:, Risky user flags, Non-Microsoft services, Scheduled tasks and Share permissions against the README. An ERROR line under a header only means that check could not run (for example a role that is not installed).

    #Fix snippets

    Each snippet runs on its own in an elevated PowerShell window. Read the numbered list above each one, check it against the README, and run only what applies.

    #Fix: domain password and lockout policy (DC)

    1. Sets minimum length 14, history 24, maximum age 60 days, minimum age 1 day, complexity on and reversible encryption off on the domain.
    2. Sets lockout after 5 bad attempts for 30 minutes, with a 30-minute counter reset.
    3. Prints the resulting policy.

    Make the Default Domain Policy GPO match too, or this reverts (why).

    Set-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy -Identity (Get-ADDomain).DNSRoot -MinPasswordLength 14 -PasswordHistoryCount 24 -MaxPasswordAge 60.00:00:00 -MinPasswordAge 1.00:00:00 -ComplexityEnabled $true -ReversibleEncryptionEnabled $false -LockoutThreshold 5 -LockoutDuration 00:30:00 -LockoutObservationWindow 00:30:00
Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy

    #Fix: clear risky AD user flags (DC)

    1. Reads every user with the Password not required, preauth and reversible encryption flags.
    2. Clears each flag where it is set and prints the user name it fixed.
    3. Disables the domain Guest account.

    Reset the password of every user listed under PNR afterwards, because clearing the flag does not set a password.

    Get-ADUser -Filter * -Properties PasswordNotRequired,DoesNotRequirePreAuth,AllowReversiblePasswordEncryption | ForEach-Object {
  if ($_.PasswordNotRequired) { Set-ADUser $_ -PasswordNotRequired $false; "PNR cleared: $($_.SamAccountName)" }
  if ($_.DoesNotRequirePreAuth) { Set-ADAccountControl $_ -DoesNotRequirePreAuth $false; "PreAuth fixed: $($_.SamAccountName)" }
  if ($_.AllowReversiblePasswordEncryption) { Set-ADUser $_ -AllowReversiblePasswordEncryption $false; "Reversible cleared: $($_.SamAccountName)" }
}
Disable-ADAccount -Identity Guest

    #Fix: MachineAccountQuota and Recycle Bin (DC)

    1. Sets ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota to 0 so ordinary users cannot join computers.
    2. Turns on the AD Recycle Bin for the forest (cannot be turned off later, which is harmless).
    Set-ADDomain -Identity (Get-ADDomain) -Replace @{'ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota'='0'}
Enable-ADOptionalFeature -Identity 'Recycle Bin Feature' -Scope ForestOrConfigurationSet -Target (Get-ADForest).Name -Confirm:$false

    #Fix: Print Spooler off (DC without printing)

    1. Stops the Print Spooler.
    2. Sets it to Disabled.

    Skip it if the README requires printing.

    Stop-Service Spooler -Force
Set-Service Spooler -StartupType Disabled

    #Fix: SMB hardening (any server)

    1. Turns SMB1 off, requires signing and turns on encryption in the SMB server configuration.
    2. Removes the SMB1 feature if it is installed.
    3. Prints the three settings so you can confirm them.
    Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false -RequireSecuritySignature $true -EnableSecuritySignature $true -EncryptData $true -Force
Get-WindowsFeature FS-SMB1 | Where-Object Installed | Uninstall-WindowsFeature
Get-SmbServerConfiguration | Select-Object EnableSMB1Protocol,RequireSecuritySignature,EncryptData

    #Fix: remove common unneeded features

    1. Lists the features to remove. Delete any name the README needs before running.
    2. Uninstalls only the ones that are installed.
    $remove = 'Telnet-Client','TFTP-Client','PowerShell-V2','SNMP-Service','Simple-TCPIP','Fax','PNRP','FS-SMB1'
Get-WindowsFeature $remove | Where-Object Installed | Uninstall-WindowsFeature

    #Fix: DNS zones (secure updates, no transfers)

    1. Selects every primary zone that is not auto-created and is not TrustAnchors.
    2. Sets AD-integrated zones to secure dynamic updates only.
    3. Turns off zone transfers on each of those zones.
    4. Prints the result.

    Skip it if the README names a secondary DNS server; set that zone to TransferToSecureServers by hand (how).

    Get-DnsServerZone | Where-Object { -not $_.IsAutoCreated -and $_.ZoneType -eq 'Primary' -and $_.ZoneName -ne 'TrustAnchors' } | ForEach-Object {
  if ($_.IsDsIntegrated) { Set-DnsServerPrimaryZone -Name $_.ZoneName -DynamicUpdate Secure }
  Set-DnsServerPrimaryZone -Name $_.ZoneName -SecureSecondaries NoTransfer
}
Get-DnsServerZone | Select-Object ZoneName,DynamicUpdate,SecureSecondaries

    #Fix: IIS basics

    1. Loads the IIS module.
    2. Turns off directory browsing server-wide.
    3. Sets every application pool to ApplicationPoolIdentity.
    4. Turns on logging for every site.
    Import-Module WebAdministration
Set-WebConfigurationProperty -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Filter 'system.webServer/directoryBrowse' -Name enabled -Value $false
Get-ChildItem IIS:\AppPools | ForEach-Object { Set-ItemProperty "IIS:\AppPools\$($_.Name)" -Name processModel.identityType -Value ApplicationPoolIdentity }
Get-Website | ForEach-Object { Set-ItemProperty "IIS:\Sites\$($_.Name)" -Name logFile.enabled -Value $true }

    #Fix: Remote Desktop hardened (README requires RDP)

    1. Requires Network Level Authentication.
    2. Requires the TLS security layer.
    3. Requires High encryption.
    Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp' -Name UserAuthentication -Value 1
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp' -Name SecurityLayer -Value 2
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp' -Name MinEncryptionLevel -Value 3

    #Fix: Remote Desktop off (README does not require RDP)

    1. Denies Remote Desktop connections.
    2. Disables the Remote Desktop firewall rules.
    Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server' -Name fDenyTSConnections -Value 1
Disable-NetFirewallRule -DisplayGroup "Remote Desktop"

    #Fix: WinRM hardened

    1. Refuses unencrypted traffic on the WinRM service.
    2. Turns off Basic authentication on the service.
    3. Does the same two things on the WinRM client.
    Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Service\AllowUnencrypted -Value $false
Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Service\Auth\Basic -Value $false
Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Client\AllowUnencrypted -Value $false
Set-Item WSMan:\localhost\Client\Auth\Basic -Value $false

    #Fix: LM and NTLMv1 off (standalone server)

    1. Sets LAN Manager authentication level 5 (NTLMv2 only, refuse LM and NTLM).
    2. Stops storing LM hashes.

    On a DC set these in the Default Domain Controllers Policy instead (how).

    Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa' -Name LmCompatibilityLevel -Value 5 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa' -Name NoLMHash -Value 1 -Type DWord

    #Fix: turn on IE Enhanced Security Configuration

    1. Sets IE ESC on for Administrators.
    2. Sets IE ESC on for Users.

    Log off and back on afterwards, or use the Server Manager toggle instead.

    Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Active Setup\Installed Components\{A509B1A7-37EF-4b3f-8CFC-4F3A74704073}' -Name IsInstalled -Value 1
Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Active Setup\Installed Components\{A509B1A8-37EF-4b3f-8CFC-4F3A74704073}' -Name IsInstalled -Value 1

    Generic Windows fix snippets (audit policy, firewall, Defender, registry values) are in Windows 11 scripts. On a DC, apply policy-type fixes through GPOs instead.

    SRV

    Server troubleshooting

    jump:srv-troubleshoot

    Fast path

    1. If the score dropped, undo your last change first; a penalty is recoverable that way (details).

    2. On a DC, check the core services from an elevated PowerShell window:

      Get-Service NTDS,DNS,Netlogon,Kdc,DFSR,W32Time,ADWS | Select-Object Name,Status,StartType

    3. Start any stopped one and set it back to Automatic:

      Set-Service <service-name> -StartupType Automatic
Start-Service <service-name>

    4. Check DC health and policy:

      dcdiag /q
gpupdate /force
gpresult /r

    5. Find your symptom below.

    #Score dropped after a change

    • Undo the last change. If the points come back, that setting, role or service was required; re-read the README.
    • Reinstall a removed role with Install-WindowsFeature <feature-name> -IncludeManagementTools, then set its services to Automatic and start them (recovery).
    • General Windows score and penalty troubleshooting is in Windows troubleshooting and scoring problems.

    #GPO change not applying

    1. Run gpupdate /force (elevated), then gpresult /r. Is the GPO under Applied Group Policy Objects, or under filtered out?
    2. Check you edited the right GPO. Password, lockout and Kerberos settings must be in a GPO linked at the domain root (Default Domain Policy). In an OU-linked GPO or the Default Domain Controllers Policy they do nothing for domain accounts.
    3. In gpmc.msc, check the link is Enabled, the GPO status is not All settings disabled, Security Filtering includes Authenticated Users (or the target), and no WMI filter excludes it.
    4. Look for a conflicting GPO with better precedence (lower link order number, or Enforced).
    5. Confirm SYSVOL and NETLOGON are shared with net share (missing).
    6. Read the logs: eventvwr.msc > Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > GroupPolicy > Operational, and the System log with source GroupPolicy.
    7. net accounts still shows old password values? Wait a minute, run gpupdate /force again, and compare with Get-ADDefaultDomainPasswordPolicy.

    #SYSVOL or NETLOGON share missing

    Check the shares and run the two dcdiag tests for them:

    net share
dcdiag /test:sysvolcheck /test:netlogons

    Restart the services that publish them:

    Restart-Service DFSR
Restart-Service Netlogon

    Then check SysvolReady under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Netlogon\Parameters. It must be 1. If someone set it to 0, set it back and restart Netlogon:

    Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Netlogon\Parameters' -Name SysvolReady -Value 1
Restart-Service Netlogon

    #Locked out after a policy change

    • Use the elevated PowerShell window you kept open to undo the change (usually a Deny logon right or Allow log on locally in the Default Domain Controllers Policy), then run gpupdate /force.
    • Account locked out: from another admin session run Unlock-ADAccount <username>. Lockout counters also reset after the observation window.
    • "Your password has expired and must be changed": change it at the prompt. It must meet the new policy, so use the team password.
    • "The sign-in method you are trying to use isn't allowed": a logon right was removed. Fix the GPO.
    • Kerberos or time errors: run w32tm /resync and check the clock. Kerberos tolerates 5 minutes of difference.
    • Last resort on a DC: restore the GPO from your backup with Restore-GPO -Name "<gpo-name>" -Path C:\GPOBackup, or reset the defaults with dcgpofix /target:Both and harden again.

    #DNS or AD broken

    Run these first:

    dcdiag /q
dcdiag /test:dns
nltest /dsgetdc:<domain-name>
ipconfig /all

    netdiag does not exist on modern Windows; use dcdiag, nltest, Resolve-DnsName and Test-NetConnection.

    Recovery steps, in order:

    1. Check the core services and fix any that are stopped or Disabled:

      Get-Service NTDS,DNS,Netlogon,Kdc,DFSR,W32Time,ADWS | Select-Object Name,Status,StartType

    2. The DC's own DNS client should point to itself. Check it, and fix it if it was changed (use 127.0.0.1 or the DC's own IP, as originally configured):

      Get-DnsClientServerAddress -AddressFamily IPv4
Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceAlias "<interface>" -ServerAddresses 127.0.0.1

    3. The AD zones must still allow Secure dynamic updates (Get-DnsServerZone), never None.

    4. Re-register the DC's records:

      ipconfig /registerdns
nltest /dsregdns

    5. Restart DNS and clear its cache:

      Restart-Service DNS
Clear-DnsServerCache -Force

    6. Turn the AD and DNS firewall rule groups back on:

      Enable-NetFirewallRule -DisplayGroup "Active Directory Domain Services"
Enable-NetFirewallRule -DisplayGroup "DNS Service"

    7. Run dcdiag /q again.

    #Bring back a role you removed

    • Reinstall with Install-WindowsFeature <feature-name> -IncludeManagementTools, then set its services to Automatic and start them.
    • IIS: sites and app pools live in C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv\config\applicationHost.config, and IIS keeps automatic copies in C:\inetpub\history. Copy the newest CFGHISTORY_*\applicationHost.config over the live one, then run iisreset. Removing the role does not delete website files in C:\inetpub\wwwroot.
    • DNS on a DC: AD-integrated zones live in AD and reappear when the DNS role is reinstalled. File-backed zones are in C:\Windows\System32\dns.
    • DHCP: the database and its automatic backup are under C:\Windows\System32\dhcp (the backup subfolder). Restore it, then restart the service:
    Restore-DhcpServer -Path C:\Windows\System32\dhcp\backup
Restart-Service DHCPServer

    #AD PowerShell module missing

    The error is "The specified module 'ActiveDirectory' was not loaded", or Get-ADUser is not recognized. Install the module and load it:

    Install-WindowsFeature RSAT-AD-PowerShell
Import-Module ActiveDirectory

    Group Policy cmdlets come with Install-WindowsFeature GPMC, DNS cmdlets with RSAT-DNS-Server, and DHCP cmdlets with RSAT-DHCP.

    #ADWS not running

    "Unable to find a default server with Active Directory Web Services running" means ADWS is stopped. Start it:

    Set-Service ADWS -StartupType Automatic
Start-Service ADWS

    #Access denied

    • Run PowerShell or cmd as administrator (right-click > Run as administrator). The title bar must say Administrator.
    • "Access is denied" when deleting or moving an AD object: clear Protect object from accidental deletion (how).
    • Group membership changes for your own account apply only after you log off and back on.
    • A file in use: stop the owning service or process first. For files opened over a share, use Get-SmbOpenFile. Sysinternals handle is not built in, and openfiles /query shows local files only if openfiles /local on was set before the last reboot.
    • Registry key denied: regedit > key > Permissions > Advanced > Owner > Administrators, then grant Full Control.
    • Defender blocks a tool you downloaded: that is Defender working. Use built-in tools instead of turning protection off.
    • File or folder denied: take ownership, then grant Administrators full control:
    takeown /f "<path>" /r /d y
icacls "<path>" /grant Administrators:F /T

    LNX

    Linux Mint master checklist

    jump:lin-checklist

    Work top to bottom and tick items as you go (the ticks are shared with the team). Each item names the command; the link goes to the section that explains it. Keep a root terminal open the whole round and write every change in your changelog so you can undo it.

    README and Forensics first

    The README on the desktop decides which users, admins, services and programs are authorized. Answer the Forensics Questions before you delete users, files or packages, because the fix can destroy the evidence. Never touch the CyberPatriot folder, the scoring report shortcut, or anything named CCS.

    #First 10 minutes

    #Users and groups

    #sudo and admin rights

    #Password policy and lockout

    #Firewall

    #Updates

    #Services and ports

    #SSH and required services

    Terminal survival on Mint

    jump:lin-terminal

    Fast path

    1. Press Ctrl+Alt+T to open a terminal.

    2. Turn it into a root shell and leave it open all round:

      sudo -i

    3. Press Ctrl+Alt+T again for a second, normal terminal. Use it to test logins and sudo after changes.

    4. Back up the config you will edit (the root shell from step 2 can run this without sudo):

      sudo mkdir -p /root/cp-backup
sudo cp -an /etc/pam.d /etc/security /etc/login.defs /etc/sudoers /etc/sudoers.d /etc/ssh /root/cp-backup/

    5. Edit with sudo nano <file>, save with Ctrl+O then Enter, quit with Ctrl+X.

    #Open a terminal

    Press Ctrl+Alt+T. From the menu: Menu > Administration > Terminal, or type terminal in the menu search box.

    A prompt ending in $ means a normal user. A prompt ending in # means root.

    #Use sudo or a root shell

    Command What it does Use it when
    sudo <command> Runs one command as root, asks for your password Normal use
    sudo -i Opens a root login shell (# prompt) Long sessions, safety net for PAM and sudoers edits
    sudo -s Root shell that keeps part of your environment Rarely needed
    exit Leaves the root shell When done
    sudo !! Re-runs the previous command with sudo You forgot sudo

    Keep one root shell open all round

    Open a terminal, run sudo -i, and never close it. If you break sudo or PAM, this shell still works, and you can put the backup back from it.

    Put passwords in single quotes, for example 'Cyb3rP@tri0t!2026'. Inside double quotes an interactive shell treats ! as history expansion and prints "event not found".

    #Edit files with nano

    Open a file as root with line numbers shown:

    sudo nano -l /etc/ssh/sshd_config
    Keys Action
    Ctrl+O then Enter Save (write out)
    Ctrl+X Exit (if asked to save: Y then Enter)
    Ctrl+W Search; Alt+W finds the next match
    Ctrl+\ Search and replace
    Ctrl+K Cut the whole line
    Ctrl+U Paste the cut line
    Alt+U Undo
    Alt+E Redo
    Ctrl+_ Go to a line number
    Ctrl+C Show the current line number

    In nano's help bar ^ means Ctrl and M- means Alt.

    #Edit files with xed

    Mint's graphical editor is xed. gedit is not installed by default.

    sudo xed /etc/ssh/sshd_config

    Save with Ctrl+S and close the window before you use that terminal again (or add & to the end of the command). Open your own files, such as Forensics answers, without sudo so the owner does not change:

    xed ~/Desktop/'Forensics Question 1.txt'

    #Back up a file before you edit it

    Copy one file next to itself before a quick edit, and copy it back if something breaks:

    sudo cp -a /etc/login.defs /root/cp-backup/login.defs.orig

    sudo cp -a /root/cp-backup/login.defs.orig /etc/login.defs

    -a keeps owner, permissions and timestamps. -n (used in the fast path) never overwrites, so running the full backup a second time keeps the original copies. If /etc/ssh does not exist, cp prints an error for it and still copies the rest.

    Start a changelog in your home folder and add one line per change, with the original value:

    nano ~/cp-changes.txt

    Keep backups out of .d folders

    Some programs read every file in their .d folder. A copy named x.bak.conf in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/ is read by sshd because it ends in .conf, and /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ reads any *.list file. sudo skips names containing . or ending in ~, and Debian cron skips names containing ., but every folder has its own rule. Keep backups in /root/cp-backup/.

    #Read and search files

    Command Use
